topics.title: Road safety, cashless care and hit-and-run compensation
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Treatment ≠ compensation
| Provision | Distinction |
| --- | --- |
| Cashless road-accident treatment | **Up to ₹1.5 lakh per victim, maximum 7 days** at designated hospitals under scheme conditions |
| Hit-and-run compensation | Separate **₹2 lakh for death; ₹50,000 for grievous injury**, 2022 scheme |
- Source January 2025 discussion follows **2024 pilot**. Pan-India **Cashless Treatment of Road Accident Victims Scheme, 2025** notified **5 May 2025**, guidelines **4 June**; do not backdate nationwide formal notification to January. [MoRTH clarification](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2153890&lang=2&reg=48), [2022 compensation notification](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1801656&lang=2&reg=48).
- Statutory basis: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 **section 162**, inserted through **2019 amendment**. Eligible accidents caused by use of motor vehicles; 'all accidents without conditions' is too broad.
- **NHA IT platform**, police, designated hospitals and state authorities; **eDAR = electronic Detailed Accident Report** supports verification/reporting. Not identical to AB-PM-JAY beneficiary insurance.
## Why and how
- **Golden hour**: first hour after injury, rapid appropriate trauma care can improve survival; emergency transport/referral and blood/trauma capacity matter.
- Good Samaritans need protection, awareness and straightforward assistance procedures.
- Official **2023** report: **1,72,890 fatalities; ages 18–45 = 66.4%**. PDF's **1.8 lakh / 18–34 = 66%** mixes rounding/age groups. [MoRTH report](https://morth.nic.in/sites/default/files/Road-Accident-in-India-2023-Publications.pdf).
- Implementation: rural access, ambulance/hospital capacity, public awareness, prompt reimbursement, coordination, fraud controls and sustainable funding; prevention complements post-crash care.

topics.title: Anaemia and AnemiaPhone
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism and causes
- **Anaemia**: low haemoglobin/oxygen-carrying capacity for the relevant group; iron deficiency is a major cause, **not the only cause**.
- Other contributors: **B12/folate deficiency**, poor intake, infections, blood loss and inherited blood disorders; nutrition and access inequalities matter.
- Fatigue, weakness, breathlessness, impaired function; severe cases can be life-threatening. Pregnancy risks include prematurity/low birthweight; signs alone do not establish the cause.
## AnemiaPhone: point-of-care iron assessment
- **Cornell University** technology licensed to **ICMR** for public-health use; announced **December 2024**, discussed in January 2025 notes. Integrates into anaemia/women's/maternal-child-health programmes; transfer is not proof of universal rollout.
- Finger-prick blood → **test strip + portable reader** → result in minutes → phone/tablet/computer-connected clinical record; source describes Bluetooth/Wi-Fi-enabled readers.
- Enables decentralised **iron-status screening**, potentially before clinical anaemia, and appropriate referral/differential diagnosis; not symptom-only smartphone diagnosis. [Cornell](https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2024/12/new-cornell-tech-evaluate-anemia-be-used-across-india).
## NFHS-5 and programme recall
- **2019–21 survey**: pregnant women 15–49 **52.2%** anaemic; children **6–59 months 67.1%**; all women 15–49 **57%**. PDF's general '50–70% pregnant / 50% children' should not replace specified survey figures. [Health Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1795421&lang=2&reg=48).
- **Anaemia Mukt Bharat, 2018**, life-cycle approach: supplementation, testing/treatment, diet/behaviour change and attention to non-nutritional causes; public-health support does not justify self-prescribing iron for every anaemia.
- Clinical workup may use CBC/haemoglobin, iron indicators and other cause-specific tests. Digital screening needs quality control, trained workers, reliable supply chains, follow-up and privacy.

topics.title: UAPA: security powers and safeguards
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Statutory distinctions
- **Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967**, MHA: unlawful activities/associations and terrorist offences; amendments include **2004, 2008, 2019**. TADA lapsed **1995**, POTA repealed **2004**; separate histories.
- Terrorist acts, financing, proceeds/property and organisational activity; law has specified extraterritorial application, not limited only to citizens inside India.
- **Unlawful-association declaration**, **terrorist-organisation listing** and **individual terrorist designation** are different processes. **2019** enabled individual designation; administrative designation is **not itself criminal conviction or an automatic detention order**.
- NIA investigates scheduled offences under its own Act; state police also have roles. Source graphic: 2019 permits **NIA Inspector-or-above** investigation in relevant circumstances and **NIA DG** approval for seizure/attachment where NIA investigates; not DGP-only for every case. [India Code](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/1470?sam_handle=123456789%2F1362).
## Custody and rights traps
- UAPA prosecution/remand is **not the same legal framework as preventive detention**. Court may extend the relevant investigation period **from 90 to 180 days subject to conditions**; not automatic indefinite custody or extensions beyond 180 merely 'after informing court'.
- Strict bail conditions, including **section 43D(5)** for relevant terrorist offences; punishments vary by offence and consequences. Graphic's 'death/life for all' and 'absolute government powers' are overstatements.
- **Article 22(1)** and written grounds of arrest: the graphic reports a police argument, not settled law. Supreme Court affirmed written grounds in **Prabir Purkayastha, 2024**; see its reaffirmation in [Supreme Court judgment](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2024/56321/56321_2024_9_1502_65444_Judgement_06-Nov-2025.pdf).
## Mains evaluation
- Need: terrorism/secession threats and disrupted financing; risks: lengthy incarceration, vague application, chilling speech and misuse allegations.
- Treat allegations involving activists/journalists/students as allegations; peaceful dissent is not by itself proof of terrorism.
- Safeguards: precise statutory grounds, evidentiary scrutiny, lawful arrest/remand, independent oversight, timely trials, reasoned review and accountability. Security and fundamental rights require effective institutions.

topics.title: India–Maldives cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 defence engagement
- **8 January 2025, New Delhi**: Rajnath Singh and Maldivian Defence Minister **Mohamed Ghassan Maumoon**; India's readiness for capability support aligned with Maldivian priorities, **Neighbourhood First** and **SAGAR**.
- Defence equipment/stores handed over on request; training, platforms, maritime security and first-responder role. [Defence Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2091162&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source discusses **Ekatha Harbour**, MNDF Coast Guard, **Sifavaru repair facility**, grant assistance and ship refit.
## Geography, partnership and interests
- Low-lying Indian Ocean coral archipelago, **~1,200 islands**, near major shipping/energy routes; climate/sea-level and disaster vulnerability.
- **Operation Cactus, 1988**: India intervened against attempted coup to support President Gayoom's government. Do not describe that government's democratic credentials uncritically as the source does.
- Defence/coast-guard capacity, anti-piracy, counterterrorism/radicalisation, humanitarian/disaster response; maritime security serves both countries.
- Food, construction materials, medicines/petroleum trade; housing, water/sanitation and infrastructure projects; tourism, education/medical travel, diaspora and cultural ties.
- **SAARC** partner; India among first to recognise independence **1965**, embassy/mission **1972** according to embedded historical graphic.
## Political context: use correct dates
- Yameen-era China ties; relations improved after **2018** change to Solih, rather than universally worsening after that election.
- **Muizzu elected 2023**, India Out debate and Indian personnel issue; subsequent rapprochement should not be described as a new leadership change after his election.
- Maumoon visit here is **January 2025**, not the text's stray 2024; Muizzu's India engagements in **2024** should not be backdated to 2023. 'China Out' phrase in source is confused.
- Embedded Yameen-era graphic's **70% debt owed to China, 25,000 Indians, 6% tourists** are undated older claims, not January 2025 statistics.
- Policy approach: respect sovereignty, reliable project delivery, people-to-people benefits and transparent financing while managing strategic competition.

topics.title: Henley Passport Index and mobility
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Methodology
- **Henley & Partners**, began **2006** as Visa Restrictions Index; based on **IATA Timatic** data and additional research.
- Source scope: **199 passports, 227 destinations**; score measures destinations accessible **without a prior visa**, not passport holders' wealth, democracy or military power.
- Distinguish ordinary visa-free access, visas on arrival and relevant electronic authorisations from **prior-approved visas/e-visas**; immigration checks still apply. A 'destination' can be a territory, not necessarily a sovereign country. [Methodology explanation](https://www.henleyglobal.com/publications/global-mobility-report/2025-january/henley-passport-index-visa-free-travel-defined).
## January 2025 snapshot
- Source **India 85th, 57 destinations**, from a cited earlier **80th**; multiple updates during a year mean different 2024/2025 releases can show different ranks.
- **Singapore 1st, 195; Japan 2nd, 193**. Source **UAE 10th** and China's longer-term **94th → 60th** are dated comparisons, not current figures. [Publisher's January release](https://www.henleyglobal.com/newsroom/press-releases/henley-global-mobility-report-january-2025%C2%A0).
- Visa rules change, and ranking depends on other passports too: a rank change does not by itself establish a proportionate change in diplomacy or geopolitical influence.
- Pandemic restrictions affected mobility after **2020**; source's 'COVID impact from 2015' is chronologically wrong.
- Mains use: mobility inequality, diaspora/business travel, bilateral visa facilitation and regional cooperation; travel ease is one indicator, not a complete measure of national power.

topics.title: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas and the Indian diaspora
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Date, origin and institutions
- **9 January** marks Gandhi's return from South Africa **9 January 1915**. First convention: **2003, New Delhi**, under Atal Bihari Vajpayee; recommendations of **L. M. Singhvi committee**, report January 2002.
- Day observed annually; major conventions **biennial since 2015**. **MEA**, host state and partner organisations; CII participation does not make it the permanent sole organiser.
- **18th convention: 8–10 January 2025, Bhubaneswar, Odisha**; PM inaugurated 9 January. Theme: **Diaspora's contribution to a Viksit Bharat**.
- Chief guest **Christine Carla Kangaloo**, President of Trinidad and Tobago, addressed virtually. [MEA overview](https://www.mea.gov.in/pravasi-bharatiya-divas.htm).
## Samman and dated examples
- **Pravasi Bharatiya Samman Award**, highest honour for overseas Indians; President confers it on eligible NRIs/PIOs and their organisations for relevant contributions.
- Source January 2025: **27 awardees across 24 countries**. Examples: **Lekh Raj Juneja, Japan—science/technology; Robert Masih Nahar, Spain—community service**, Indian-origin Spanish senator since 2017 and cricket promotion; **Syed Anwar Khursheed, Saudi Arabia—medical service**, royal-protocol physician. [MEA award overview](https://www.mea.gov.in/pravasi-bharatiya-samman.htm).
- Source diaspora snapshot **over 3.5 crore**; USA **54 lakh**, UAE **35 lakh**, Canada **28 lakh**, Saudi Arabia **24 lakh**. Reference dates unspecified; not current population counts.
- Source remittance estimate **$125 billion in 2023**; distinguish remittances from foreign investment and diaspora headcount.
## Diaspora → contribution → policy
- Remittances, trade/investment, innovation, skills, philanthropy, cultural networks and public diplomacy; **Howdy Modi, Texas, 2019**, with Donald Trump, illustrates outreach.
- PM's January 2025 themes: developed India **2047**, humanity-first approach, Global South, African Union's G20 inclusion, Ashoka/Dhauli and Buddhist peace heritage.
- Preserve **Girmitiya/indentured-labour histories** through research and databases; historic Mandvi–Muscat commercial links described as about **250 years old**. Cultural memory complements present-day economic ties.
- Policy balance: consular protection, worker welfare, diaspora participation and host-country sovereignty; overseas Indian identity does not automatically confer Indian citizenship or voting rights.

topics.title: Wildfires: drivers, impacts and management
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## California: January 2025 case
- Los Angeles-region fires included **Palisades, Eaton and Sunset**; source maps highlight coastal/urban areas around Malibu, Los Angeles and Hollywood.
- Source's developing-news snapshot: **7 deaths and over 10,000 structures affected/destroyed**; an earlier embedded report cites **2 deaths and about 70,000 evacuations**. Different report times, not final totals or numbers to add together.
- Dry vegetation, low rainfall, drought conditions and strong **Santa Ana winds** intensified spread; dry downslope winds warm through compression and rapidly carry embers. Hilly terrain can accelerate uphill spread.
- [CAL FIRE's 11 January Eaton update](https://www.fire.ca.gov/incidents/2025/1/7/eaton-fire/updates/a1fb81e4-a242-45d9-b001-0dc25f174d01) describes dry northeast winds and Red Flag conditions.
## Fire triangle and amplification
| Required factor | Examples / control |
| --- | --- |
| Heat / ignition | Lightning, electrical faults, careless burning or deliberate arson; ignition control |
| Fuel | Dry grass, shrubs, forest litter and buildings; defensible space/fuel management |
| Oxygen | Air; wind also transfers heat/embers and changes fire behaviour |
- **Arson is intentional**, not accidental. General possible ignitions do not establish the investigated cause of a particular fire.
- Climate conditions influence fire weather and fuel dryness; attributing any single fire entirely to climate change requires evidence. Urban expansion into the **wildland–urban interface** increases exposure.
## Impacts and response
- Deaths/displacement, homes/infrastructure lost, habitat damage, soil erosion and polluted runoff; smoke particulates aggravate respiratory and cardiovascular illness. Insurance affordability/availability and livelihood recovery are policy concerns.
- **Before**: satellite/drone detection, fire-weather warning, power-line safety, zoning/building codes, fuel breaks and professionally planned prescribed burns.
- **During**: evacuation routes, accessible warnings, trained crews, water/retardants with environmental safeguards; protect responders and vulnerable residents.
- **After**: safe return, ash/water monitoring, erosion control, habitat restoration, transparent relief and resilient reconstruction.
- Mains: prevention + land-use planning + preparedness + ecosystem-sensitive recovery; emergency suppression alone is insufficient.
## Pink aerial retardant: January 2025
- **Phos-Chek** is a brand of long-term fire retardants, generally ammonium-phosphate/polyphosphate-based formulations. Pink colour marks treated ground; it is not the extinguishing mechanism.
- Water carrier evaporates → retardant remains → vegetation combustion/spread slowed → supports ground response. Weather, flight safety and placement limit performance; an aerial drop is not guaranteed to extinguish a severe wildfire.
- Source's Los Angeles death figure rose to **24** by its January 13 reporting; earlier figure stays dated, not a contradictory final toll.
- Some formulations tested contain **chromium/cadmium and other toxic metals**; exposure/aquatic risk differs by product and dose. A study estimated **850,000 pounds of metals** released in the western US **2009–2021**, not all retardant chemicals globally since 2009. [USC research summary](https://viterbischool.usc.edu/news/2024/10/toxic-metals-found-in-wildfire-suppressants/).
- Balance emergency protection with safer formulations, waterway protection, careful application and environmental monitoring; don't generalise one tested product to every Phos-Chek formulation.

topics.title: Sonamarg / Z-Morh tunnel
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Location and purpose
- **Gagangir–Sonamarg, Ganderbal, Jammu and Kashmir**, on **Srinagar–Leh NH-1**. Name **Z-Morh** refers to a Z-shaped road stretch; terrain above **8,500 feet**, prone to snow/avalanches.
- Main tunnel **6.4 km in official release**; source rounds to **6.5 km**. Project includes an **egress tunnel and approach roads**, approximately **12 km overall**.
- Source specifications: two-lane road, designed around **1,000 vehicles/hour**, **80 km/h**; cites **4.26-km escape** and **0.6-km ventilation** components. Escape passage is for emergencies, not ordinary parallel traffic.
- **11 January 2025** announcement: inauguration scheduled **13 January**; subsequently inaugurated that day. [PMO announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2092091&lang=2&reg=48), [inauguration](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2092468).
## Corridor recall
- **Srinagar → Gagangir → Sonamarg → Zoji La → Drass/Kargil → Leh**. Distinct from **Banihal–Jammu NH-44**.
- Sonamarg tunnel enables all-weather access to Sonamarg; alone it does **not** complete year-round access across every Ladakh bottleneck.
- Separate **Zojila tunnel**, source **14.15 km**, planned eastward connection across the pass; do not confuse its length/completion with Sonamarg.
- Benefits: winter tourism, local livelihoods, rescue and defence logistics near sensitive northern/eastern frontiers; monitor ecological disturbance, avalanche risk and emergency ventilation/egress.
## Practice-test trap
- The 19 January key overstates year-round access to all of Ladakh. **Sonamarg access ≠ completion of the separate Zoji La tunnel**; check the specific section of the route.

topics.title: Workplace ethics, overwork and duty of care
topics.subject: Ethics
topics.markdown:
## Case and ethical questions
- Source discusses **Anna Sebastian Perayil, 26, EY employee**: her mother's allegations of excessive work pressure and insensitive organisational response. Treat alleged causation/responsibility as allegations, not a proved medical or judicial finding.
- Long hours, unrealistic expectations, fear of retaliation and insecure performance assessment can erode dignity and health; wellness branding must match daily management practices.
- Relevant values: **duty of care, empathy, fairness, integrity, accountability, dignity and confidentiality**. Credit misappropriation and silencing grievances undermine trust.
## Claim → evidence → judgement
- Source debate over **18 hours/day for 4–5 years** and demands for **70-hour weeks**: productivity cannot be assumed proportional to hours; fatigue, error, inequality and health costs matter.
- Entrepreneurial autonomy/reward and salaried employees' bargaining power differ; entrepreneurship is not automatically a safe or feasible remedy for overwork.
- **WHO–ILO study published 2021** estimated **745,000 deaths in 2016** from stroke/ischaemic heart disease attributable to **≥55 working hours/week**, globally—not India alone or a count of every cause of overwork death. [WHO–ILO findings](https://www.who.int/news/item/17-05-2021-long-working-hours-increasing-deaths-from-heart-disease-and-stroke-who-ilo).
## Ethical management flow
- **Identify excessive demand → assess health/workload risks → redistribute or resource work → protect rest and grievance access → review outcomes**.
- Leaders: realistic deadlines, adequate staffing, fair credit/compensation, confidential counselling, non-retaliation, documented escalation and empathetic support after crises.
- Employees: communicate constraints, record concerns, seek support and use safe reporting channels; individual resilience cannot replace organisational duty.
- Evaluate actual workload, grievance resolution, turnover and wellbeing rather than counting wellness events. Voluntary overtime/pay does not remove the need for safe conditions.
- Mains conclusion: success includes health and dignity; reconcile performance with sustainable work and accountable leadership.

topics.title: Gaddi dog and indigenous breed conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Himalayan guardian
- **January 2025**: **ICAR–National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources**, Karnal, recognised Gaddi as a registered indigenous dog breed; source calls it the **fourth** after **Rajapalayam, Chippiparai (Tamil Nadu)** and **Mudhol Hound (Karnataka)**. This is a dated registration count.
- Named after **Gaddi shepherds, Himachal Pradesh**; guards sheep/goats against predators. Nicknames **Indian Panther Hound / Indian Leopard Hound** reflect guarding ability, not a taxonomic relationship with cats.
- Mainly Himalayan; predominantly **black**, occasional white feet/tail/trunk, strong arched neck and muscular, moderately long body.
- Registration documents breed characteristics and supports conservation, suitable breeding and avoidance of genetic erosion; no automatic wildlife protection schedule follows from breed registration.

topics.title: Soapstone / steatite
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Rock → mineral → formation
- **Soapstone / steatite**: talc-rich **metamorphic rock**; **talc is a mineral**, not every soapstone specimen is pure talc. Soft, dense and heat-resistant; talc contributes the soapy feel.
- Associated minerals vary: **mica, chlorite, amphibole, quartz, magnesite and carbonates**.
- Heat/pressure and alteration of **peridotite, dunite or serpentinite**; chemically active hot fluids can alter **siliceous dolostone**, an example of **metasomatism**. Convergent settings favour metamorphism; not the only formation setting.
- Graphic recall: temperature/pressure change existing rocks without requiring complete melting; melting and solidification would instead produce igneous rock. [NPS rock classification](https://home.nps.gov/subjects/geology/metamorphic.htm).
## Locations, uses and regulation
- January 2025 source: Uttarakhand High Court scrutiny of unregulated mining in **Bageshwar**, cited **over 160 mines**; slope stability, river pollution and compliance are governance concerns.
- Source lists **China, India, Brazil, USA and Finland** among producers; Indian Bureau of Mines reserve snapshot **Rajasthan 57%, Uttarakhand 25%**, reference year unspecified; not current market shares.
- Slabs: countertops, sinks, hearths and sculpture. Processed talc: ceramics, paint, roofing, cosmetics/pharmaceutical formulations, lubricating/filling/thickening uses.
- Source describes talc/corn-starch powders; this is an industrial-use fact, not advice to apply mineral dust to infants. Product purity and inhalation/contamination risks require appropriate standards.

topics.title: Sonobuoys and undersea domain awareness
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 cooperation
- India–USA **co-production of sonobuoys** for Indian Navy **Undersea Domain Awareness (UDA)**; complements submarine tracking and anti-submarine warfare.
- **Expendable electro-mechanical acoustic sensors**; aircraft/helicopters deploy canisters in patterns. Surface float/radio antenna communicates while **hydrophone/sensors descend to a selected depth**.
- **Deploy → listen/emit → transmit → analyse contacts → locate/track**. Multiple measurements improve localisation; detection is not automatically a perfect position fix.
| Type | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Passive | Listen to target/environment sounds; no active sonar pulse |
| Active | Emit acoustic energy and analyse returning echoes |
| Special purpose | Measure temperature, ambient noise and other environmental conditions |
- Components: buoyant housing, sensors/hydrophone, battery/power and radio/data link to aircraft/ship.
- Applications: detect/classify and support engagement of adversarial submarines/ships; oceanographic/environmental research and marine-mammal acoustic monitoring.
- Prelims trap: **sonar uses sound**, not radar radio waves to travel through deep water; radio link is generally above-water communication.

topics.title: UJALA and efficient lighting
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Design
- **Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All**, launched **5 January 2015**; earlier **Domestic Efficient Lighting Programme (DELP)**. Energy efficiency, not a renewable-generation scheme.
- **EESL with DISCOMs**, Ministry of Power; large-scale **zero-subsidy** LED distribution, bulk procurement/e-procurement and competitive pricing.
- Source eligibility: households with metered electricity connections; upfront payment or instalment arrangements where offered; **SHGs** participate in distribution.
- LED price cited **₹300–350 → ₹70–80** through scale and market transformation; programme-era comparison, not a current retail quote.
## 6 January 2025 snapshot
| Indicator | Source / official snapshot |
| --- | --- |
| Distributed LED bulbs | **36.87 crore** |
| Annual electricity saved | **47,883 million kWh** |
| Annual monetary saving | **₹19,153 crore** |
| Peak demand reduced | **9,586 MW** |
| Annual CO₂ reduction | **3.87 crore tonnes** |
- [Power Ministry's ten-year review](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2090639&lang=1&reg=1). Savings estimates are annual, not cumulative generation.
- Source's **85 lakh kWh / 15,000 tonnes CO₂** target lacks a usable timeframe and is inconsistent in scale with reported achievements; don't memorise it as the national annual target.
- **77 crore conventional bulbs** is a replacement ambition; **3.5 crore streetlights** belongs to the separate street-lighting programme, not household bulbs already distributed under UJALA.
- Mains mechanism: pooled demand → lower unit cost → wider adoption → lower electricity demand/bills/emissions; verify quality, disposal and access.
## Practice-test trap
- UJALA household bulbs and the **Street Lighting National Programme (SLNP)** are separate programmes. Do not attribute cumulative streetlight replacements to UJALA merely because both use LEDs.

topics.title: Toda: society, livelihood and embroidery
topics.subject: Anthropology
topics.markdown:
## Nilgiri community
- **Nilgiri Hills, Tamil Nadu**; hamlet **mund**. Source describes a language without a traditional script; oral language does not mean absence of linguistic complexity.
- **Patrilineal descent**; source's two endogamous divisions **Tharthazoll and Theveioll**. Clan names given: **Paiki, Pekkan, Kuttan, Kenna and Todi**; transliterations vary.
- Traditional council **Noim**, headman **Monegar**, social regulation/dispute settlement; do not interpret traditional authority as unlimited legal power overriding Indian law.
- Buffalo pastoralism and embroidery; sacred buffalo/dairy associations make livelihood and ritual closely connected.
- **Red-and-black embroidery on white cloth**, GI-protected **Toda Embroidery, Tamil Nadu**. [GI register](https://search.ipindia.gov.in/GIRPublicSearch/Application/Details/135).
- **Modhweth**, New Year/buffalo festival; source places observance on last Sunday of December or first Sunday of January.
- Anthropology recall: **descent ≠ residence ≠ marriage rule**; patriliny alone does not establish every household's residence practice. Preserve culture with community participation, livelihood security and language transmission.
## Practice-test correction
- The 19 January Noim answer letter contradicts its own explanation. Recall **traditional council/social dispute resolution**, with authority subject to Indian law; reject claims of unrestricted powers.

topics.title: Kalpeni atoll and coral formation
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map and landforms
- **Lakshadweep, Arabian Sea**; **southeast of Kavaratti**, between **Andrott and Minicoy**, about **287 km / 155 nautical miles from Kochi**.
- Official/source area **2.79 km²**; north–south alignment; lagoon maximum width **about 2.8 km**, not its total area.
- **Kalpeni + Tilakkam + Pitti + northern Cheriyam** form an atoll; **Cheriyam** described as uninhabited, not Kalpeni itself. [Administration geography](https://lakshadweep.gov.in/islands/kalpeni/), [atoll constituents](https://lakshadweep.gov.in/tourist-place/kalpeni/).
- **Volcanic island/fringing reef → subsidence with upward coral growth → barrier reef/lagoon → ring-like atoll**: classic schematic, not proof each island has an identical geological history.
- Coral reefs shelter lagoons and support diverse marine life; tourism includes snorkelling/diving; Kerala-like maritime monsoon climate.
## January 2025 news and correction
- Divers reported wreckage possibly from a **17th/18th-century European warship**; identity/date were provisional, not an authenticated archaeological conclusion.
- Source's **Maliku community** label confuses Kalpeni with **Minicoy/Maliku**; administration distinguishes Malayalam-speaking islands from Minicoy's **Mahl** language. [Lakshadweep islands](https://lakshadweep.gov.in/islands/).
- Protect reefs and wreck sites: scientific investigation, visitor limits, waste control and community livelihoods; avoid souvenir removal or unverified heritage claims.

topics.title: Garudakshi: digital forest-crime management
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Karnataka pilot: January 2025
- Forest Department online forest-offence/FIR system, developed with **Wildlife Trust of India**; encroachment, illegal felling, poaching and unauthorised entry.
- Pilot divisions: **Bengaluru Urban, Bhadravathi, Sirsi and Male Mahadeshwara Wildlife Sanctuary**; not nationwide implementation.
- Modules: **legacy case registration → online offence registration → investigation → reporting/analytics**; generates report/complaint formats, public complaints via mobile/email.
- Source says portal registration compulsory on implementation; digitisation supports enforcement under applicable forest/wildlife laws without automatically changing their substantive offences.
- Benefits: standard records, faster tracking, pattern detection and accountability; safeguards: data quality/security, trained staff, access for people without smartphones and verification of complaints.

topics.title: Vultures and toxic veterinary drugs
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Nimesulide: correct regulatory scope
- **NSAID**, pain/inflammation medicine. Veterinary exposure can damage vulture kidneys; **visceral gout** indicates uric-acid deposition associated with renal failure.
- **Medicated livestock → contaminated carcass → scavenging vulture → kidney injury → gout/death**; highlights indirect ecological effects of pharmaceuticals.
- **S.O. 5633(E), 30 December 2024**, section **26A, Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940**: **nimesulide/formulations for animal use** prohibition. **20 February 2025** CDSCO circular sought enforcement. [CDSCO record](https://www.cdsco.gov.in/opencms/opencms/en/Notifications/Gazette-Notifications/), [enforcement circular](https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/resources/UploadCDSCOWeb/2018/UploadPublic_NoticesFiles/Nimesulide%20and%20its%20formulatin.pdf).
- January source's blanket assertion that this makes all human administration banned/unsuitable is unsupported; human-use safety restrictions are a separate issue. No medical-use recommendation follows from this note.
- Source lists earlier veterinary use in cattle/pigs/horses and human pain/fever indications; these describe usage, not endorsed prescribing.
- Conservation: enforce veterinary-drug restrictions, monitor carcass exposure, safe alternatives under professional guidance and vulture-population recovery; scavengers provide ecosystem sanitation services.

topics.title: GenomeIndia: reference genomes and precision medicine
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Programme and January 2025 milestone
- **DBT-funded multi-institution consortium**, initiated **2020**; large-scale sequencing to represent Indian genetic diversity. January 2025 data milestone builds on earlier sequencing announcements. [PMO address, 9 January 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2091506&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source: **10,074 samples across 99 ethnic groups**, approximately 10,000 genomes; **5,750** refers to an analysis subset, not a competing whole-project total.
- Data housed at **Indian Biological Data Centre, Faridabad, Haryana**; research access requires appropriate safeguards, not unrestricted release of named individuals' medical records.
## What the reference enables
| Objective | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Variation catalogue | Common, low-frequency and rare variants; **SNPs** and structural variants |
| Haplotype reference | Variants inherited together; supports statistical imputation of missing variants |
| Genome-wide arrays | Affordable research/diagnostic tools suited to represented populations |
| Biobank | Stored **DNA/plasma** for approved future research |
- **Sample → sequence → quality checks/joint genotyping → reference database → validated research/clinical applications**.
- Potential: disease-risk research, pharmacogenomics, precision medicine and host susceptibility to infections; association does not guarantee diagnosis or cure.
- Ethics: informed consent, privacy, secure access, representative sampling, benefit sharing and avoiding caste/ethnic determinism or genetic discrimination.

topics.title: International Organization for Migration
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- Founded **1951**, headquarters **Geneva, Switzerland**; intergovernmental migration organisation, **UN related organisation**. Not interchangeable with UNHCR's refugee-protection mandate.
- Humane/orderly migration, cooperation, practical migration management and humanitarian assistance to migrants, including displaced/refugee populations where relevant.
- Coordinates **UN Network on Migration**; source says 'coordinator for Secretary', which should not be memorised as the formal role.
- Labour mobility/human development work: policy and operations, diaspora-development links and integration. Supported **Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration, 2018**; the compact is not a binding refugee convention.
- Source membership **175 members, 8 observers** is an undated snapshot; membership changes. Publications: **World Migration Report**, **Migration Health Annual Report**.
## January 2025 Syria appeal
- Expanded earlier **$30 million** appeal to **$73.2 million**, response period **December 2024–May 2025**; humanitarian funding requested, not money already received. [IOM flash appeal](https://mena.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl686/files/documents/2025-01/iom-flash-appeal-for-syria-dec-2024-may-2025.pdf).
- Mains: reconcile dignity/protection, host capacity, safe mobility, integration and international burden sharing.

topics.title: Polar vortex and cold-air outbreaks
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Concept and distinctions
- Broad polar **low-pressure/cold-air cyclonic circulation**. Distinguish **stratospheric polar vortex** from upper-tropospheric circulation/jet patterns; they interact but are not one identical vertically uniform feature.
- Winter strengthens the stratospheric vortex; summer weakening/breakdown is part of its seasonal cycle. Source's 'always exists unchanged from tropopause through mesosphere' is too sweeping across both definitions.
- Normal cyclonic circulation: **anticlockwise in Northern Hemisphere**, **clockwise in Southern Hemisphere**; not anticlockwise at both poles.
- **Jet streams**: narrow fast winds in upper troposphere near tropopause; source approx **30,000 feet / 9.1 km**, height varies.
## Strong containment → disturbance → possible surface effects
- Strong circulation helps contain polar air; disturbances/weakening/displacement can alter jet patterns and favour some midlatitude cold outbreaks.
- A stratospheric disruption is **not required for every cold spell**, nor a guarantee all regions turn cold; coupling, timing and local weather matter. [NOAA distinctions](https://prod-01-asg-www-climate.woc.noaa.gov/news-features/blogs/enso/polar-vortex-going-make-you-put-sweater-be-afraid-be-very-afraid), [NWS cold-air explanation](https://www.weather.gov/safety/cold-polar-vortex).
- Source January 2025 US cold outbreak; Europe/Asia also affected in relevant events. Southern circulation tends to be more symmetric, with ocean-dominated surroundings; Southern Hemisphere cold outbreaks still occur.
- Impacts: hypothermia/frostbite, transport disruption, agricultural losses and energy demand; forecasts and protection for vulnerable people matter.
## Precision trap
- The **stratospheric** polar vortex is principally a winter feature; the tropospheric circulation persists year-round. Avoid an undifferentiated claim that every polar vortex remains equally strong in every season.

topics.title: Ebola: transmission, prevention and treatments
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Disease recall
- Severe viral disease; **Orthoebolavirus genus, Filoviridae**. First recognised **1976**, outbreaks in **Yambuku, now DRC**, and **Nzara, now South Sudan**; Ebola River gave the name.
- Fruit bats, particularly **Pteropodidae**, implicated as natural hosts; humans and other primates can become ill.
- Infected animal exposure → spillover; human transmission through **direct contact with infected bodily fluids/tissues**, sick/dead persons or contaminated materials. Not principally mosquito-borne or ordinary airborne transmission.
- Incubation **2–21 days**; fever, weakness, vomiting/diarrhoea and sometimes bleeding; bleeding is not universal. Average case-fatality **about 50%**, varies widely by outbreak/access to care.
## Correct the treatment claim
- Source's 'no fully tested treatments' conflicts with established therapies: **Inmazeb / REGN-EB3** and **Ebanga / ansuvimab / mAb114**, monoclonal-antibody treatments for **Zaire/Ebola virus disease**, recommended by WHO in **2022**.
- These do not constitute an approved treatment for every orthoebolavirus disease. Licensed vaccines also target particular viruses; **Ervebo** is not a universal all-strain Ebola vaccine. [WHO treatment guidance](https://www.who.int/news/item/19-08-2022-who-makes-new-recommendations-for-ebola-treatments-----calls-for-improved-access), [WHO disease distinctions](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/ebola-disease).
- Early supportive care, fluids/electrolytes and symptom management improve survival; blood products used when clinically appropriate, not compulsory for every patient.
- Source reports **nanobody-based inhibitors** as research; experimental discovery is not proof of approved population-wide therapy.
- Response: detection/testing, isolation with safe care, contact tracing, PPE/infection control, safe dignified burials and vaccination where relevant; survivors need follow-up and non-stigmatising support.

topics.title: Siachen: geography, strategic control and altitude risks
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Map and historical anchor
- **Karakoram, northern Ladakh**; glacier near India–Pakistan–China territorial interfaces, **Saltoro Ridge** to its west, **Nubra Valley** connection southward.
- Source's 'largest glacier outside polar regions' is incorrect: NASA describes Siachen as **second-longest midlatitude glacier**, not the world's largest non-polar glacier. [NASA geography](https://eol.jsc.nasa.gov/Collections/EarthObservatory/articles/SiachenGlacier.htm).
- Source approximately **75 km** refers to glacier/sector length, not a surveyed joint 75-km India–Pakistan–China border; avoid conflating glacier length with boundary length.
- **Operation Meghdoot, 13 April 1984**, secured strategic glacier/Saltoro heights ahead of anticipated Pakistani action; not simply reclaiming territory after an already-completed Pakistani occupation. [Defence Ministry account](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2017834&lang=2&noshow=1&reg=48).
## Cold + altitude + logistics
- High posts may reach **20,000–23,000 feet**; glacier's entire length is not uniformly at these elevations. Extreme winter/source range **−20°C to −60°C** varies by place/time.
- Falling pressure → **lower oxygen partial pressure** → hypoxia; oxygen's atmospheric percentage stays broadly similar, not progressively replaced by another gas.
- Risks: altitude illness, cold injury, snowstorms/avalanches, sleep disturbance, appetite/weight loss, impaired memory and difficult casualty evacuation.
- Response: acclimatisation, suitable clothing/shelter, nutrition, medical monitoring, oxygen/evacuation capacity and reliable logistics; claiming survival is universally impossible without acclimatisation is too absolute.
- Source's recovered **Malkhan Singh**, aircraft crash **7 February 1968**, illustrates prolonged ice preservation and recovery challenges; the crash story is separate from Operation Meghdoot and Siachen's border history.

topics.title: Gulf of Mexico: map, resources and naming
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map recall
- Atlantic marginal sea on southeastern North America; bordered by **USA, Mexico and Cuba**, world's largest gulf; sometimes called **Mediterranean of the Americas**.
| Connection | Passage |
| --- | --- |
| Gulf ↔ Atlantic | **Straits of Florida**, between Florida and Cuba |
| Gulf ↔ Caribbean | **Yucatán Channel**, between Yucatán Peninsula and Cuba |

## Dated naming development
- January 14 source: President-elect Trump proposed **Gulf of America**.
- **20 January 2025 executive order** subsequently directed US federal geographic-name changes for the described US continental-shelf area and agency references. It does not itself redraw maritime boundaries or impose nomenclature on Mexico/Cuba. [Executive order](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/01/restoring-names-that-honor-american-greatness/).
- Prelims trap: **Florida → Atlantic; Yucatán → Caribbean**, not the reverse. A political naming change does not alter physical geography.

topics.title: WMO and the 2024 temperature record
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- **World Meteorological Organization**, **UN specialised agency**, founded **1950**; predecessor **International Meteorological Organization, 1873**. Headquarters **Geneva, Switzerland**.
- International cooperation in meteorology, hydrology, climatology and related geophysics; atmosphere–ocean interactions, climate and water resources.
| Body | Role |
| --- | --- |
| World Meteorological Congress | Supreme policy body, normally four-year cycle |
| Executive Council | **36 members**, annual sessions, implements Congress decisions |
| Secretariat | Administration; Secretary-General appointed for **four-year term** |
- Source **193 members = 187 States + 6 Territories**, January 2025 snapshot; members are not all sovereign states.
## 2024 record: interpret carefully
- January 2025 WMO synthesis of **six international datasets**: **2024 warmest year on record**, global mean near-surface temperature **about 1.55°C ± 0.13°C above 1850–1900**.
- A **single calendar year above 1.5°C** does not itself establish that the Paris Agreement's long-term warming threshold has been permanently crossed. Dataset differences and natural variability affect yearly estimates.
- Distinguish **weather event**, **annual anomaly**, and **long-term climate warming**; base period must accompany a temperature anomaly. [WMO announcement](https://wmo.int/news/media-centre/wmo-confirms-2024-warmest-year-record-about-155degc-above-pre-industrial-level).
- Mains: emissions mitigation, adaptation/early warning and climate-resilient water, food, health and infrastructure policy.

topics.title: Pangolins and Indo-Burmese taxonomy
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species proposal: January 2025
- ZSI-associated research described **Manis indoburmanica**, Indo-Burmese pangolin, as distinct from **Chinese pangolin (M. pentadactyla)** and **Indian pangolin (M. crassicaudata)**.
- Source locations: **Arunachal Pradesh/Assam**, possible Nepal, Bhutan and Myanmar extension; **180–1,830 m**; dark/olive-brown scales, pinkish face. A predicted range is not confirmed presence everywhere.
- Source reports **8% genetic difference** and **3.4-million-year divergence**; metrics/methods not supplied, so don't treat these as definitive universal figures.
## Later taxonomic clarification
- **1 July 2026** genomic/morphological study revalidated **Manis aurita Hodgson, 1836**, treating **M. indoburmanica** as a junior synonym under naming priority; estimated separation from M. pentadactyla **about 1.8 million years**.
- Keep **2025 proposal** separate from **2026 revision**: lineage evidence, species delimitation and the oldest valid scientific name are related but different questions. [Primary research](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42003-026-10314-9), [Mammal Diversity Database](https://www.mammaldiversity.org/taxon/1006934/).
## General recall and conservation
- **Order Pholidota, family Manidae**; Africa/Asia; unique mammalian **keratin-scale armour**. Curl into a ball; long sticky tongue; **myrmecophagous**, ants/termites.
- Many dig burrows; **fossorial ≠ arboreal**, and behaviour varies across pangolin species.
- Source's traditional **8 species: 4 African + 4 Asian** count predates/does not resolve newer taxonomic revisions; avoid adding the new name to eight without checking whether it replaces an older taxon.
- Severe trafficking for scales/meat and habitat loss; scale demand in traditional medicine is not evidence of medicinal effectiveness.
- Graphic's traditional Asian species: **Indian, Chinese, Sunda and Philippine**; African: **giant, Temminck's ground, white-bellied and black-bellied**.

topics.title: Foot-and-mouth disease
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 outbreak
- **Water buffalo near Berlin, Brandenburg, Germany**; first German occurrence since **1988**, officially notified **10 January 2025**, not an unspecified exactly 40-year interval. [WOAH statement](https://www.woah.org/en/statement-on-recent-foot-and-mouth-disease-fmd-outbreak-in-germany/).
## Pathogen, hosts and spread
- Highly contagious **Aphthovirus, Picornaviridae**, livestock disease; cattle, pigs, sheep, goats and other susceptible **cloven-hoofed animals**. Horses/dogs/cats are not usual susceptible hosts.
- **Seven serotypes: O, A, C, SAT1, SAT2, SAT3, Asia1**; immunity/vaccines are not universally interchangeable across serotypes or all strains.
- Animal secretions/excretions, aerosols, direct contact and contaminated equipment/clothing; people can mechanically carry virus without having the livestock disease.
- Fever, mouth/tongue/lip/teat/interdigital blisters → lameness, salivation, poor intake; weight loss, growth retardation and persistent milk-production loss. Adult deaths generally low; young animals may die from severe disease/myocarditis.
- Transboundary disease: trade restrictions and major production losses. Source **77% of world livestock** refers to population in areas where disease circulates, not a measured 77% simultaneously infected.
## Prevention and traps
- Matched vaccines, surveillance/rapid notification, biosecurity, movement controls, outbreak response and appropriate official disease-status procedures; first disease for which WOAH established official status recognition.
- **Livestock FMD ≠ human hand-foot-and-mouth disease**; not ordinarily a human-health/food-safety threat. [WOAH disease information](https://www.woah.org/en/disease/foot-and-%20mouth-disease/).
- Intensive husbandry can amplify spread; traditional breeds are not automatically immune. Graphic **Futvac** is a vaccine example, not a universal vaccine name for all serotypes.
## Precision trap
- **Seven serotypes** does not mean only seven viral strains: multiple strains/subtypes occur within serotypes.

topics.title: Desert National Park and Great Indian Bustard
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Location and ecosystem
- **Thar, Rajasthan, Jaisalmer and Barmer districts**; **about 3,162 km²**, source rounds to over 3,160. [Rajasthan protected-area record](https://forest.rajasthan.gov.in/content/raj/forest/en/aboutus/departmental-wings/wildlife/details-of-protected-area-.html).
- Arid landscape: rocky outcrops, salt-lake bottoms, interdunal areas, fixed dunes and open desert grass/scrub; **dunes about 20%**, not 50%. Source **under 100-mm annual rainfall** is not a universal park-wide climatic threshold.
- **Human settlements occur within the landscape**; conservation must account for pastoral/local livelihoods.
- **Great Indian Bustard**, critically endangered; source sighting of **12** is a local observation, not a national population estimate or by itself proof of population recovery.
- Other source fauna: **chinkara, desert/Bengal fox, Indian wolf, desert cat, hare, spiny-tailed/monitor lizards, saw-scaled viper**. Broad reptile lists do not prove every species equally abundant at every site.
- **Khejri, Prosopis cineraria**, ecological/cultural importance, including Bishnoi conservation traditions; regional fossil-rich geological heritage, Jurassic-era deposits cited.
## Correct misplaced park details
- **Rajbagh, Malik Talao and Padam Talao** are associated with **Ranthambore**, not lakes to memorise for Desert National Park. Source's **Dhok/Ronj/Salai/palm** list also mixes generic/other-park flora; prioritise desert vegetation and verified local records. [Ranthambore management plan](https://forest.rajasthan.gov.in/content/dam/raj/forest/ForestDepartment/PDFs/Department%20Wing/Wildlife/tigerconservationplan/TCP%20RTR.pdf).
- GIB conservation: habitat connectivity, low-disturbance breeding areas, safe power-line planning and community partnership; balance infrastructure with bird survival.
## UPSC Prelims 2020
- Statements: **(1) spread over two districts—correct; (2) no human habitation—incorrect; (3) natural habitat of GIB—correct**. Answer **(c) 1 and 3 only**; full question in common Environment PYQ-Prelim JSON.

topics.title: Crude oil imports and energy security
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## December 2024 source snapshot
- Pre-February 2022: Iraq/Saudi Arabia major suppliers; after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, discounted Russian crude reshaped sourcing.
- Source explanation for December shift: Russian refinery utilisation after maintenance and domestic/seasonal demand constrained exports; West Asian supplies gained share.
| Supplier | December 2024 imports | Change / basket share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Russia | **1.48 million barrels/day** | **−17%**; share **38% November → 31.5% December** |
| Iraq | **1.13 million b/d** | **+29%**; **18.7% → 24%** |
| UAE | **530,000 b/d** | **+22.1%**, 32-month high; **9.2% → 11.2%** |
| Saudi Arabia | **649,000 b/d** | **+4.4%**; **13.8% December** |
- Differentiate **supplier's volume** from **share of India's import basket**; these are source-period data, not today's shares.
## Prices → sourcing → macro effects
- Source **Urals about $5.5/barrel below Arab Light**, **Basrah Medium about $0.80 above Dubai benchmark**; different grades/benchmarks, time-specific spreads.
- Landed cost includes freight, insurance, sanctions/payment constraints and refinery suitability; the largest discount alone does not determine supply.
- Source India **over 85% import dependence**, third-largest oil consumer; distinguish crude-import dependence from all-energy dependence.
- Oil prices/import bill → current account, rupee, inflation, fiscal/subsidy pressures and transport/industrial costs. Diversification, strategic reserves, efficiency and cleaner alternatives strengthen energy security.
- Source predicts weak Russian supplies early 2025 and possible **March–April 2025** rebound during refinery maintenance; forecasts, not verified subsequent outcomes.

topics.title: Election records, transparency and public trust
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## What changed in December 2024?
- **Conduct of Elections (Second Amendment) Rules, 2024**, **S.O. 5517(E), 20 December 2024**; made under **Representation of the People Act, 1951, section 169**, after consultation with ECI.
- **Rule 93(2)(a)**: inserted **“as specified in these rules”** after “papers”, narrowing the category open to inspection under that provision. This is an ordinary statutory-rule amendment, **not a constitutional amendment**. [Gazette text](https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2024/259568.pdf).
- Debate concerns non-prescribed electronic records such as CCTV/webcasting. Do not equate it with abolition of **Form 17C**, which is prescribed, or cancellation of copies supplied to polling agents under the applicable rules.
- **Form 17C** records votes at a polling station; polling agents receive copies. Public online access, candidate-agent access and judicial access are distinct questions. [ECI explanation](https://www.eci.gov.in/evm-faqs).
## Competing considerations
- Transparency/accountability and voter confidence versus voter privacy, ballot secrecy, security and risk of decontextualised disclosure.
- Source raises turnout-revision concerns in **Odisha, Haryana, Maharashtra** and invokes **Chandigarh mayor election**, litigation and **2024 electoral-bonds judgment**; allegations/editorial conclusions are not findings that manipulation occurred in each named election.
- **Article 324**: ECI's supervision/direction/control; neutral administration and reasoned disclosure bolster trust. A challenge being filed does not itself invalidate the rule or establish a final court outcome.
## Mains response
- Publish timely, reconciled aggregate data and explain provisional/final differences; preserve auditable records and candidate safeguards.
- Clearly define access categories/retention, protect identities/ballot secrecy, provide secure redacted access where lawful, independent review and grievance remedies.
- Evaluate amendment through proportionality, statutory authority and constitutional values; distinguish reform recommendations from existing enforceable disclosure duties.

topics.title: PM-KISAN: income support and eligibility
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Scheme recall
- **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi**, launched **February 2019**, effective from **December 2018**; **Central Sector**, 100% Union funding, **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**.
- **₹6,000 annually in three ₹2,000 instalments**, direct transfer to eligible **landholding farmer families**; States/UTs identify eligible beneficiaries and verify land records.
- Initially small/marginal farmer scope; expanded irrespective of holding size **subject to exclusion criteria**. Source's 'all landholding farmers' without exclusions is incomplete. [Official scheme](https://pmkisan.gov.in/), [2019 expansion](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1576233&lang=2&reg=48).
- Institutional landholders and specified higher-income categories excluded; tax-paying/professional/public-office categories assessed under scheme guidelines. Tenancy without qualifying recorded land ownership does not automatically create entitlement.
- Objective: supplement input/household liquidity and reduce distress borrowing, not reimburse the full cultivation cost or provide crop insurance.
- Issues: land-record errors, exclusion of vulnerable cultivators, timely transfer, grievance resolution and real value of assistance; DBT does not by itself resolve eligibility inequity.

topics.title: Plasticisers and esterase bioremediation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Research recall
- **EstS1 esterase**, from soil bacterium **Sulfobacillus acidophilus**: laboratory research on breakdown of **phthalate plasticisers**; enzyme structure studied by **X-ray crystallography**. Reported activity over roughly a month concerns tested conditions, not guaranteed field performance.
- Plasticisers are **additives** that impart flexibility/durability; removing them is different from destroying the plastic **polymer backbone**. Exposure can occur through leaching from products, food/contact materials and personal-care items; health effects depend on substance, dose and exposure.
- **DEHP: bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate** → ester hydrolysis → **MEHP: mono(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate + 2-ethylhexanol**. A monoester intermediate may remain harmful; first-step hydrolysis is not complete detoxification/mineralisation.
- Other bacterial enzymes, including research on **Comamonas testosteroni**, can take intermediates through **phthalate → hydroxylated intermediates → protocatechuate → central metabolism**, eventually CO₂/water under suitable conditions. Multiple steps/organisms may be needed.
- Source suggests polymer-binding could help remove contaminants from water. Do not infer demonstrated complete **polypropylene biodegradation** from binding or plasticiser degradation. [EstS1 primary research](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0969212624004969).
## Persistence graphic: approximate estimates
| Item | Source estimate |
| --- | --- |
| Plastic bag / coffee cup | **20 / 30 years** |
| Straw / six-pack ring | **200 / 400 years** |
| Bottle / plastic cup | **450 years** |
| Coffee-mixing pod / disposable nappy / toothbrush | **500 years** |
- These are illustrative environmental-persistence estimates, not fixed experimentally universal lifetimes. Sunlight, temperature, oxygen and medium matter; fragmentation into **microplastics ≠ complete biodegradation**.
- Mains: source reduction, safer substitutes, segregated collection, producer responsibility and verified treatment; enzymes complement rather than replace waste prevention.
## Practice-test correction
- EstS1 is linked to **plasticiser degradation**, not methane absorption. The 19 January printed answer points to the wrong listed application.

topics.title: Organ donation, NOTTO and donor leave
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Organisation and law
- **National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation (NOTTO)**, under **DGHS, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**; apex coordination of donation/transplant networks and donor/recipient registries under the national programme.
- **Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994**, amended **2011** to incorporate tissues and related regulation; consent, lawful allocation and prevention of commercial exploitation matter.
| Division | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| National Human Organ and Tissue Removal and Storage Network | Network/coordination and information functions |
| National Biomaterial Centre / National Tissue Bank | Tissue banking, quality and demand–supply coordination |
- Donation recall: **kidneys, liver, heart, lungs, pancreas, intestine**; tissues such as **cornea, skin, bone, heart valves and blood vessels**. Living donation and deceased donation differ; not every organ can be donated by a living person.
## Leave: dated rule
- **DoPT order, 25 April 2023**: up to **42 days special casual leave** for eligible **Central Government servant organ donors**, subject to medical recommendations and prescribed conditions.

topics.title: Trichophyton indotineae and antifungal resistance
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Pathogen and transmission
- **Dermatophyte fungus**, named **Trichophyton indotineae in 2020**, following study of isolates from India/Nepal. A geographic name does not establish where all infections originated.
- Causes itchy, inflamed **tinea/ringworm** skin lesions, often widespread across groin, buttocks, trunk or face; dermatophytes as a group can affect skin, hair and nails. **Ringworm is fungal, not a worm**.
- Contact with affected skin and contaminated towels/clothes; source reports detection in over **40 countries** and renaming advocacy by over **30 dermatologists in 14 countries**, January 2025 figures.
## Resistance and public health
- Often **terbinafine-resistant**; not every isolate resists every antifungal. Misuse of topical steroid–antifungal–antibiotic combinations can mask/worsen infection and contributes to the problem.
- Correct diagnosis, species/resistance surveillance, appropriate clinician-led treatment and antifungal stewardship; avoid treating a source regimen as personal medical advice. [CDC investigation](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/72/wr/pdfs/mm7219a4-h.pdf).
- Naming ethics: precise scientific communication without stigmatising a country/community.

topics.title: Hattee community and Boda Tyohar
topics.subject: Anthropology
topics.markdown:
## Community and geography
- **Boda Tyohar**, major annual festival of the **Hattee/Hatti**, **Trans-Giri, Sirmour district, Himachal Pradesh**.
- Name associated with selling agricultural/wool produce at a **haat**. Related communities across **Jaunsar-Bawar, Uttarakhand**; **Giri and Tons**, Yamuna-system rivers; Tons forms sections of the Himachal–Uttarakhand boundary.
- Traditional community council **khumbli**; ceremonial white headgear; agriculture and cash crops. Do not relocate the community to Kinnaur/Lahaul-Spiti because a generic Himachal economy paragraph mentions those districts.
- Source **2011 population about 2.5 lakh**, later roughly **3 lakh** estimate without a specified census year: preserve dates/estimate status.
## Scheduled Tribe status
- **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Act, 2023**, inserted **“Hattee of Trans Giri area of Sirmour district”** in Himachal's list; geographic scope matters. It is an ordinary Act amending the ST Order, not a numbered constitutional amendment. [Gazette Act](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/repealedfileopen?rfilename=A2023-14.pdf).
- Source contrasts **Jaunsar-Bawar recognition in 1967**; don't assume every group using a similar name everywhere automatically has identical legal status.

topics.title: Vice-Chancellor appointments and federalism
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 draft
- **Draft UGC teacher/academic-staff qualification and higher-education standards Regulations, 2025**, released **6 January 2025**. These notes describe the **proposal**, not assume it is today's operative rule.
- Proposed eligibility: **ten years** as professor, senior research/academic administrator, or senior industry/public administration/public policy/PSU professional with significant academic/scholarly contributions.
| Proposed search committee | Nominating authority |
| --- | --- |
| Chairperson | **Visitor / Chancellor** |
| Expert | **UGC Chairman** |
| Expert | **University apex body**, e.g. Senate/Syndicate/Executive Council |
- Visitor/Chancellor constitutes committee and appoints from its **3–5-name panel**. Independence, conflicts/recusal and transparent selection matter. [Official draft, section 10](https://www.ugc.gov.in/pdfnews/3045759_Draft-Regulation-Minimum-Qualifications-for-Appointment-and-Promotion-of-Teachers-and-Academic-Staff-in-Universities-and-Colleges-and-Measures-for-the-Maintenance-of-Standards-in-HE-Regulations-2025.pdf).
## Existing framework versus proposal
- Earlier UGC norms call for eminent higher-education experts and a **panel of 3–5 candidates**; this panel size is not automatically the number of committee members.
- University Acts/statutes differ: President is Visitor of many central universities; Governor commonly Chancellor of state universities by **statute**, not an automatic constitutional power over every university. Source central/State/private examples are not a uniform all-India committee formula.
- Source conflicts: **Kerala** reappointment/Chancellor replacement; **West Bengal** interim VCs and Supreme Court-linked search process; **Tamil Nadu** search nominees and appointment Bills; **Karnataka** proposed changes for six universities; **Maharashtra** reversal of earlier restrictions. Legislative/court positions are dated January 2025, not current outcomes. Kerala's earlier controversy involved **Arif Mohammed Khan**; avoid calling him its January 2025 Governor.
## Federal balance: mains frame
- Union **List I Entry 66**: coordination/determination of higher-education standards; **Concurrent List Entry 25**: education, subject to relevant Union entries. Education shifted to Concurrent List by **42nd Amendment, 1976**.
- National quality/merit and wider talent pool versus State autonomy, local accountability and financing; centrally nominated members do not automatically prove political misconduct.
- Consult States; clarify statutory authority; independent expert selection, recorded reasons, disclosure of conflicts and timely appointments; assess NEP 2020 goals alongside federal safeguards.
## Statutory power and precedent: January 2025 debate
- **UGC Act, 1956, section 26** authorises regulations within the Act's purposes. Whether specific VC rules adequately relate to educational standards is a legal question; an editorial claim of overreach is not itself a judgment invalidating the draft.
- **Suresh Patilkhede**, Bombay High Court (source labels **2011**): cited for doubts about applying UGC VC criteria to State statutory appointments; distinguish High Court reasoning from the full Supreme Court line of authority.
- **Kalyani Mathivanan v. K.V. Jeyaraj, 2015**: source incorrectly describes blanket mandatory application to all State universities. The ruling distinguished the 2010 framework's mandatory central/institutional operation from its directory character for relevant State institutions pending State adoption; Tamil Nadu had not adopted the scheme. Do not extrapolate this mechanically to every later regulation. [Supreme Court's subsequent discussion, paragraph 35 onward](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2024/45256/45256_2024_8_1501_62293_Judgement_14-Jul-2025.pdf).
- **Articles 246/254** and legislative competence/repugnancy must be read alongside **Entry 66, List I** and **Entry 25, List III**. A State law versus delegated central rule dispute is not settled simply by saying either government always wins.
- UGC prescribes standards/selection norms; **final appointment authority arises from applicable university law**, commonly Chancellor/Visitor. A UGC search nominee is not direct UGC appointment of every VC.

topics.title: Denotified and nomadic communities: SEED and inclusion
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Categories and exclusion
| Category | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **DNT** | Communities denotified after colonial criminal-tribe labelling |
| **NT** | Nomadic livelihoods/mobility |
| **SNT** | Semi-nomadic, periodically mobile |
- **Criminal Tribes Act, 1871** imposed collective stigma; denotification/repeal **1952**. Mobility and denotification are different criteria; categories overlap.
- Communities may be classified **SC, ST, OBC or none** depending on State/list; examples **Kanjar, Nat, Pardhi, Sapera**. Neither all STs nor all nomads are automatically DNTs.
- Identity/address documentation and certificates, insecure housing/livelihoods, interrupted schooling, healthcare access, stigma and limited representation; source's claim that none ever owned land/property is overbroad.
## Commissions: timeline recall
- **1947 Criminal Tribes Inquiry**; **1949 Ananthasayanam Ayyangar committee**; **1953 Kalelkar Commission**, first Backward Classes Commission.
- **Mandal** appointed **1979**, report **1980**; **NCRWC 2002** examined stigma; **Renke** constituted **2005**, report **2008**; **Idate** decision **2014**, report titled **2017**, submitted **8 January 2018**.
- Source lists **1,526 communities, 269 unclassified**; a 2022 official summary lists **1,262**. Different catalogues/counts should not be treated as one consistent current census. Population claims **25 crore**, **10%**, **10–12 crore**, and **150 DNT/500 NT groups** also differ in scope/period and are estimates, not settled present census totals.
## SEED and welfare
- **Scheme for Economic Empowerment of DNTs**, launched **February 2022**, Social Justice and Empowerment Ministry; planned **₹200 crore over five years from 2021–22**.
| Component | Delivery link |
| --- | --- |
| Competitive/professional entrance coaching | Education/employment access |
| Health insurance | **PM-JAY** |
| Livelihoods | **NRLM / State Rural Livelihood Missions** |
| Housing | **PMAY** |
- **DWBDNC**, registered society, established **21 February 2019**, rather than a permanent statutory commission. [Board record](https://dwbdnc.dosje.gov.in/index.php/content/about-us).
- **Dr Ambedkar pre/post-matric scholarships** and **Nanaji Deshmukh hostel scheme**, **2014–15**, source focus on DNT students outside SC/ST/OBC coverage. Eligibility/overlapping benefits require scheme-specific checks.
- Idate recommendations: permanent commission; State welfare departments; detailed survey; classification of unclassified groups; legal safeguards, including proposed additional SC/ST atrocities-law schedule. **Recommendations are not enacted protections by themselves**. [Official SEED background](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2022/feb/doc202222519501.pdf).
## Mains response and PYQs
- Documentation camps/portable entitlements → accurate identification → accessible education, healthcare, housing and livelihoods → anti-stigma enforcement → participation and outcomes audit. Avoid treating mobility as criminal propensity.
- **Prelims 2014, Changpa**: primarily **Ladakh**, rear **pashmina goats**, **ST**; statements **2 and 3**, answer **(b)**. This comparison does not classify all Changpa as DNTs.
- **Mains 2017** asks for two major post-Independence legal initiatives addressing ST discrimination (**250 words, 15 marks**). Full questions are in the common subject PYQ files; welfare schemes and enforceable anti-discrimination laws must be distinguished.

topics.title: Hollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary and NBWL
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Sanctuary and primates
- **Jorhat, Assam**; approximately **100–120 m** altitude; terrain gently slopes southeast → northwest. **Bhogdoi River** supports waterlogged/semi-hydrophytic habitat at its border.
| Forest layer | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Upper canopy | **Hollong** |
| Middle canopy | **Nahar** |
| Lower layer | Evergreen shrubs/herbs |
- Hoolock gibbons: India's only wild **apes**, **family Hylobatidae**, arboreal/diurnal, long arms and **brachiation**; territorial calls and pair bonding. Male dark with pale brows, female generally brown/buff. **Not monkeys**.
- Source graphic's traditional species: western **Hoolock hoolock**, **Endangered**; eastern **H. leuconedys**, **Vulnerable**, CITES **Appendix I**, dated graphic categories. Traditional range includes Northeast India/Myanmar and, for western, Bangladesh; species boundaries/ranges can be revised. Graphic's **20 gibbon species / 25-year lifespan** are approximate dated recall, not immutable counts.
- **Bengal slow loris**, Northeast India's nocturnal primate; not the only nocturnal primate everywhere in India.
- Source fauna: elephants, tiger/leopard, jungle cat, wild boar, civets, squirrels; **stump-tailed, northern pig-tailed, rhesus and Assamese macaques**, capped langur. Presence list is not a current population census.
## January 2025 exploration approval
- **Standing Committee of NBWL** approved proposed oil/gas **exploration in the sanctuary's eco-sensitive zone**, not unrestricted commercial production inside the sanctuary. Environmental, wildlife and other required clearances remain distinct. [Parliamentary explanation](https://eparlib.sansad.in/bitstream/123456789/2989605/1/lsd_18_IV_06-02-2025.pdf).
- **NBWL: section 5A, Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**, chaired by **Prime Minister**, Environment Minister vice-chair; source membership **47**.
- **Standing Committee: section 5B**, chaired by **Environment Minister**. Do not give the two bodies the same chair.
- Habitat diversion, protected-area boundary changes and relevant tourism proposals face statutory safeguards; tiger-reserve changes also involve **NTCA** and applicable legal processes. NBWL does not alone erase every safeguard.

topics.title: Cockfighting: law, tradition and animal ethics
topics.subject: Ethics
topics.markdown:
## Issue and law
- Cockfighting pits roosters against each other, sometimes with sharp blades/spurs; injury/death and associated unlawful betting. Source discusses Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala; customary popularity does not confer legal exemption.
- **Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960**, notably **section 11(1)(m)/(n)** provisions concerning entertainment involving fighting and organising places for animal fights. [Act text](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/7233/1/awbi01.pdf).
- Source cites **IPC 428/429**: these dealt with mischief by killing/maiming animals, not every unnecessary-pain offence. For January 2025, IPC references are historical: **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, section 325**, operates from **1 July 2024**, subject to offence facts. [BNS](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/20062/1/a202345.pdf).
- Source's 2017 Supreme Court narrative concerns enforcement of the Andhra Pradesh prohibition; avoid reading it as an independently verified blanket new national ruling on every animal sport.
- **PETA = People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals**; PETA India and its expanded name are not two unrelated organisations.
## Ethics: values → action
| Competing claim | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Cultural continuity / livelihoods | Respect communities; provide lawful alternatives |
| Animal welfare | Prevent avoidable suffering and lethal entertainment |
| Rule of law | Consistent enforcement, fair procedure, curb unlawful gambling |
| Public responsibility | **Article 51A(g)**: compassion for living creatures |
- Engage local leaders, run awareness campaigns, support nonviolent festival competitions and alternative livelihoods, and enforce anti-cruelty laws without selective tolerance.
- Tradition is relevant context, not a sufficient ethical defence of cruelty; evaluate harm, legality, compassion and practical alternatives together.

topics.title: Trade deficit and external-sector resilience
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Concepts: keep the balances separate
- **Merchandise trade balance = goods exports − goods imports**; negative means a merchandise deficit. Goods + services balance differs; **current account** also includes primary income and transfers/remittances. **Trade deficit ≠ fiscal deficit ≠ current-account deficit**.
- Causes: crude oil dependence (**over 85%**), electronics/semiconductor inputs and pharmaceutical **APIs**, notably from China; domestic investment/demand, relative prices, competitiveness and global demand.
- Imported capital/intermediate goods can raise productivity/exports; consumers gain choice, competition can stimulate efficiency. Benefits of imports do not prove that any size of persistent deficit is sustainable.
## Dated December 2024 data
| Merchandise | December 2024, USD bn |
| --- | --- |
| Exports | **38.01**, about **−0.99%** year-on-year |
| Imports | **59.95** |
| Deficit | **21.94**, rounded to 22 in graphic |
- Source graphic April–December exports **316.6 → 322.5**, imports **506.6 → 540.3**, deficit **190 → 217.8**, USD bn; these differ from the revised official January release: **exports 321.71, imports 532.48, deficit 210.77** for April–December 2024. Use matching revised series, not a mixture. [Commerce Ministry release](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/archiveContent.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=266125).
- Embedded graphic December growth: imports **gold +55.39%, petroleum +2.21%, silver +210.97%, electronics +9.60%**; exports **petroleum products −28.62%, gems/jewellery −26.51%, chemicals −2.93%**, non-oil exports **+5.05%**. Period/base matter; these are dated source figures.
## Effects: conditional, not automatic
- Import competition can displace some jobs; inputs can create others. Persistent external imbalances may pressure rupee/import prices and create financing risk.
- **FDI/equity inflows, borrowing or reserves** can finance external imbalances; a trade deficit does not automatically mean foreign borrowing or reserve depletion. Services/remittances can offset goods deficits. [RBI balance-of-payments framework](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/PublicationsView.aspx?id=9479).
- Source's emphasis on lost **export-duty revenue** is misleading as a general fiscal mechanism: most exports are not subject to export duty. Broader growth/tax effects vary.
## Policy and mains structure
- Competitive logistics/ports, reliable power, quality/innovation, skills and diversification; domestic capability in critical inputs; export-market access through negotiated FTAs, including **India–UAE CEPA**.
- Public procurement and carefully targeted import substitution can help; blanket high tariffs can raise input costs, harm exports and invite retaliation. FTA benefits depend on rules of origin/utilisation, not automatic bilateral balance.
- Answer sequence: define correct balance → explain composition/drivers → weigh productive imports against vulnerability → address competitiveness, energy diversification and stable financing.
- The source's daily mains prompt is **coaching practice**, not a dated UPSC PYQ.

topics.title: Robotic MULES and military autonomy
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Platform and purpose
- **MULE: Multi-Utility Legged Equipment**, quadrupedal unmanned ground robot associated with **AeroArc/ARCV**, Delhi; displayed at **77th Army Day, Pune, 15 January 2025**. Theme **Samarth Bharat, Saksham Sena**. Army Day recalls **K. M. Cariappa's command takeover, 1949**.
- Legs traverse stairs, slopes and debris; sensors/thermal cameras support reconnaissance/perimeter security, light supply carriage, hazardous-material handling and possible bomb-disposal support. Payload options are not proof every deployed unit has every attachment or weapon.
| Technical recall | Qualification |
| --- | --- |
| Weight / payload / top speed | **51 kg / 12 kg / 3 m/s** |
| Computing / protection | **NVIDIA Xavier / IP67** |
| Endurance | **About 3 hours walking**, **20–21 hours standby**, not 20 hours continuous movement |
| Temperature | Product page gives **−40°C to +55°C** in narrative, **−45°C** lower limit in feature list; tested specification/version needs checking |
- Manufacturer lists modular cameras, robotic arm, chemical/radiation detection and weapon-system options. [AeroArc product specifications](https://aeroarc.in/products/). The **100-km command range** in coaching text lacks supporting product specification here.
## Dated procurement claims and evaluation
