- Source places delivery of **100 units in June 2023** before its stated **September 2023 order**; inconsistent sequence, not a verified procurement timeline. It cites emergency procurement ceiling **₹300 crore**, which is not evidence of actual contract value.
- Pune was a first Pune parade, not the first ever outside Delhi; source merges parade and Southern Command investiture contexts. [Official Army Day report](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2093060&lang=2&reg=3).
- Benefits: reduce human/canine exposure, carry small loads, improve situational awareness; potential disaster-response/search-and-rescue uses.
- Limits: endurance, payload, communications loss, terrain reliability, cyber security and maintenance. An armed autonomous-capable robot requires human accountability, lawful targeting and appropriate control; autonomy does not establish independent lethal deployment.
- Indian assembly/vendor presence alone does not establish wholly indigenous hardware, software or IP.

topics.title: Jallikattu: culture, welfare and law
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Tradition and debate
- Tamil Nadu **Pongal**, January harvest festival; bull-taming event. **Jalli**: coins; **kattu**: tied—traditional prize associated with the bull's horns.
- Agrarian identity, bravery, human–animal relationships; supporters link breeding value to indigenous **Kangayam, Pulikulam, Bargur** cattle. Conservation benefit is an argument to evaluate, not proof every event protects biodiversity.
- Risks: bull stress/injury, tail twisting/poking/drugging, participant/spectator injury; rural livelihoods and cultural continuity must be weighed against preventable harm.
## Legal timeline: correct the source
| Year | Development |
| --- | --- |
| **2014** | **AWBI v A. Nagaraja**: Supreme Court prohibited Jallikattu under the then law; highlighted animal welfare/compassion |
| **2017** | Tamil Nadu amended the **Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960**, with rules permitting regulated Jallikattu |
| **18 May 2023** | Constitution Bench upheld relevant Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra amendments concerning Jallikattu, Kambala and bullock-cart racing |
- January 2025 source incorrectly calls constitutional validity still undecided. The 2023 decision requires statutory safeguards; it is not blanket permission for cruelty. [Supreme Court judgment](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2016/1216/1216_2016_3_1501_44624_Judgement_18-May-2023.pdf).
- **Article 51A(g)** compassion; **48** animal husbandry, **48A** environmental/wildlife protection; cultural claims invoke **29**. Do not treat source's Article 21 reference as an unqualified holding that animals have the same enforceable fundamental rights as persons.
- Wildlife protection legislation is not the central regulating statute for a domestic bull sport. Mains: cultural participation with independent welfare inspection, veterinary checks, safety barriers, accountability and enforcement.
## Breed trap
- **Gir is indigenous to India (Gujarat)**. A breed being outside the typical Tamil Nadu Jallikattu breed list does not make it foreign to India.

topics.title: Nagarahole, chital and prey–predator balance
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Reserve map
- **Mysuru and Kodagu, Karnataka**; landscape connectivity with **Wayanad Sanctuary, Kerala**, south, and **Bandipur**, southeast; Western Ghats/Nilgiri forest landscape.
- Scrub and deciduous forests with other moist habitats. Calling the Western Ghats a UNESCO site does not mean every site/entire reserve is automatically a listed component.
- Fauna: tiger, leopard, dhole, sloth bear; **chital, sambar, gaur, four-horned antelope, elephant**; southwestern langur.
## Dated population interpretation
- January 2025 report: **28 chital/km²**, source **142 tigers**, described as third-highest reserve population in a 2023 release. Keep survey area/method/year distinct; these are not today's counts.
- Adequate prey supports predators, but density alone does not establish a perfectly balanced/healthy ecosystem. Food/water, habitat, disease, grazing pressure, seasonal change and survey uncertainty matter.
- Habitat diversity/grass availability, controlled livestock grazing and protection can support prey; camera-trap and other systematic monitoring inform management. Tigers outside core areas may imply landscape use/conflict risk, not automatically beneficial overflow.
## Chital recall
- **Axis axis**, spotted deer, native to the Indian subcontinent, **Least Concern** in source. Reddish-brown coat/white underparts, persistent white spots; social herds, source typical **10–50**.
- Males larger; males carry **three-tined antlers**, shed annually; antlers differ from permanent horns.
- Source approximate size **35 inches/89 cm**, **187 lb/85 kg**, antlers near **3 ft/91 cm**; dimensions vary with sex/age/population. The printed **20–30-year lifespan** should not be treated as a verified typical wild lifespan.
- Distribution graphic lists India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Bhutan and small Pakistan occurrence; distinguish native range, introduced populations and locally extinct occurrences.

topics.title: Kashi Tamil Sangamam and Agasthyar
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Edition 3.0, 2025
- **15–24 February 2025**, **Namo Ghat, Varanasi**, during the wider Maha Kumbh period; Kumbh's main venue **Prayagraj**, not Varanasi.
- Theme: **Sage Agasthyar's legacy**—Tamil language/literature, philosophy, knowledge and health traditions; strengthen cultural/intellectual ties between Tamil Nadu and Kashi.
- Source planned **1,200 delegates**, five groups: students/teachers/writers; farmers/artisans; professionals/small entrepreneurs; women; startups/innovation/edtech/research. Separate **200 Tamil-origin Central-university students**, youth participation encouraged. [Education Ministry programme](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2102893&lang=2&reg=48).
## Links: history versus tradition
- Agasthyar's foundational role in Tamil knowledge is a **traditional attribution**, not a precisely dated proof of sole authorship of a language.
- **Brahmanda Purana** narrative of Dasharatha seeking Kamakshi's blessings at Kanchipuram: religious tradition, not independently established chronology.
- Source **15th-century Parakrama Pandya** and Sivakasi temple story; **Kasi Viswanathar Temple, Tenkasi** recalls north–south religious links. Distinguish temple history from journey legends.
- **Varanasi–Kanchipuram silk trade** and pilgrimage support people-to-people exchange. Evaluate inclusion, multilingual learning and sustained exchanges rather than only delegate numbers.

topics.title: Blue Ghost, Resilience and commercial lunar missions
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## One rocket, two missions
- **15 January 2025**, **SpaceX Falcon 9**, Kennedy Space Center, Florida: **Firefly Aerospace Blue Ghost (USA)** and **ispace Resilience (Japan)** rideshare launch.
| Lander | January plan |
| --- | --- |
| Blue Ghost | Roughly **45-day journey**, **10 NASA instruments**, **Mare Crisium near Mons Latreille**, northeastern near side |
| Resilience | Roughly **4–5 months**, **Mare Frigoris**, northern lunar region; **Tenacious micro-rover**, ispace-Europe |
- Blue Ghost is a **NASA CLPS** delivery, supporting science/technology and Artemis goals; sharing its launcher does not make the Japanese mission itself a NASA CLPS contract.
- Investigations: dust, lunar interior, Earth magnetosphere interactions, radiation-tolerant navigation/computing; rover/regolith handling for Resilience. [NASA payloads](https://science.nasa.gov/lunar-science/clps-deliveries/to19d-firefly/).
## Landing and dated outcomes
- Essentially no atmosphere → **parachutes cannot provide Earth-like braking**; powered descent/navigation must avoid rocks/craters. Rideshare saves launch cost but does not guarantee landing success.
- Later: **Blue Ghost landed 2 March 2025**; **Resilience's June 2025 attempt failed**, communication lost/no successful landing. Keep launch intentions separate from outcomes. [ispace update](https://www.ispace-inc.com/2025/06/06/status-update-on-ispace-mission-2-smbc-x-hakuto-r-venture-moon/).
- **Intuitive Machines** achieved the first commercial soft landing in **2024**; commercial providers complement national agencies, not eliminate their role in science/funding/regulation.
## Country recall
- **Intuitive Machines is American**, not Chinese; Blue Ghost → Firefly/USA, Resilience → ispace/Japan. Nationality of company differs from launch provider.

topics.title: Natural catastrophe losses and insurance resilience
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Hazard × exposure × vulnerability
- Swiss Re report cited: India **2023 economic losses about US$12 bn**, versus **US$8 bn annual average over the prior decade**. Economic loss differs from insured claims; more exposed assets can increase losses without a matching increase in hazard frequency.
- Source attributes roughly **63%** of annual catastrophe economic losses over two decades to floods; **Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu 36.8% industrial output** cited, baseline unspecified. Industry concentration raises exposure, not identical risk everywhere.
- **Protection gap** concerns losses not covered by insurance. Source's **over 90% households/businesses uninsured or underinsured** should not be substituted for a verified census of households: original insurance analysis may use loss-based denominators.
| Dated event | Location / correction |
| --- | --- |
| North India floods, July 2023 | Himachal Pradesh/Delhi and wider northern region |
| Sikkim disaster | Major **October 2023 glacial-lake outburst**, not simply the same July flood |
| Biparjoy, June 2023 | Gujarat/Kutch landfall, port/transport disruption; peak-category label need not equal landfall intensity |
| Michaung, December 2023 | Flooded Chennai; **landfall near Bapatla, Andhra Pradesh, 5 December**, not Chennai |
- Source examples **Mumbai 2005 US$5.3 bn**, **Chennai 2015 US$6.6 bn** are inflation-adjusted estimates; coaching says 2024 prices while Swiss Re graphic specifies **2023 prices**. Don't compare nominal/adjusted losses without a common base. [Swiss Re January report](https://www.swissre.com/dam/jcr%3A4c54602e-f24f-4322-8e8a-bfd6ada77062/2025-01-14-swiss-re-%2520institute-expertise-publication-india-economy-and-insurance-market.pdf), [IMD Michaung bulletin](https://rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in/uploads/archive/48/48_a0b4ee_15.%20Hourly%20Bulletin%2005122023-0800%20UTC.pdf).
## Resilience: prevention plus risk finance
- Southwest monsoon **June–September** (Kerala 2018/Uttarakhand 2013 examples), northeast monsoon **October–December** (Chennai 2015); Gujarat cyclone/earthquake/flood risks, Mumbai flood/cyclone exposure, Chennai coastal/urban-flood risk. Delhi, Ahmedabad and Himalayas face seismic hazards.
- Granular hotspot mapping → recent-data exposure/risk modelling → mitigation + insurance/reinsurance tailored to remaining risks.
- Land-use/drainage, resilient buildings, early warning/evacuation and ecosystem protection; accessible policies, affordable premiums, clear exclusions and reliable claims. Insurance transfers financial risk; it does not prevent deaths or physical damage.

topics.title: India–Bangladesh border fencing
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Border map and incident
- **4,096.7 km**, India's longest land boundary with a neighbour; **West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
- Plains, hills, forests and rivers: source's claim of **no natural obstacles** conflicts with its riverine-terrain discussion.
- January 2025 disputes: **Kaliachak III, Malda** and **Mekhliganj/Cooch Behar near Dahagram–Angarpota**, **10 January** incident; diplomatic summons **13 January**. **BSF** versus **Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB)**.
- Source fencing **3,141 km** and Bengal **81.5% as of 2023** are dated; not full fencing. About **900 km riverine stretch** cited, physical fencing difficult; surveillance alternatives vary by terrain.
## Agreements and competing claims
- **1975 joint guidelines**, **150-yard** restriction concerning defence structures; disagreement over classification of wire/single-row fencing and agreed exceptions. Don't turn either party's legal claim into a settled finding of breach.
- India: fence deters illicit movement/cattle smuggling/trafficking; Bangladesh: proximity and CCTV/smart-surveillance objections. A fence does not itself change the international boundary.
- Challenges: land acquisition, settlements/cross-border access, difficult terrain, pending consent/negotiations; source blames State non-cooperation, but this is an attributed explanation, not proof of sole responsibility.
- Solution: joint surveys/flag meetings, documented consent where required, phased land/access arrangements, sensitive riverine monitoring and proportionate enforcement respecting residents' rights.

topics.title: Gaza ceasefire: January 2025 agreement
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Background and casualty correction
- **7 October 2023 Hamas-led attack**, Israeli military response, hostage captivity and grave civilian humanitarian losses. Distinguish armed actors from entire civilian populations.
- Source Israel **over 1,200 deaths** and about **100 remaining hostages**, dated approximations.
- Coaching's **over 64,000 Gaza deaths** is inconsistent with the January snapshot: OCHA cites Gaza MoH **46,645 reported fatalities as of 14 January 2025**, with casualty verification qualifications; roughly **1.9 million displaced, 90% of Gaza**. [OCHA dated snapshot](https://www.ochaopt.org/sites/default/files/Gaza_Reported_Impact_Snapshot_14_January_2025.pdf).
## Three phases: agreement is not guaranteed completion
| Phase | Intended steps |
| --- | --- |
| **1: six weeks** | Ceasefire; **33 hostages** exchanged for Palestinian detainees/prisoners; Israeli pullback from populated areas; return of displaced people; aid target **600 trucks/day** |
| **2** | Remaining living hostages; further prisoner exchange; full withdrawal/permanent cessation negotiated |
| **3** | Return of deceased hostages' remains and reconstruction |
- January 17 source describes pending Israeli Cabinet approval. **Ceasefire began 19 January 2025**; phase one lasted to **1 March**. This does not establish all later phases implemented. [UN response review](https://www.ochaopt.org/content/report-humanitarian-response-un-and-humanitarian-partners-during-phase-one-ceasefire).
- Obstacles: sequencing, verification, prisoner/hostage categories, security conditions, domestic coalition pressures, access and reconstruction finance. Source's claim that war strengthened one politician is commentary, not a settled causal fact.
- Mains: protect civilians, lawful humanitarian access, credible monitoring, return/reconstruction and negotiated durable political settlement.

topics.title: Small language models
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## SLM versus LLM
- Language models process/generate text; **parameters** are learned numerical weights, distinct from training tokens. “Small” is relative—no universally fixed cutoff.
| SLM tendency | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Fewer parameters / compact architecture | Lower memory/compute, possible on-device operation |
| Curated data / task adaptation | Efficient target tasks; narrower coverage can limit generalisation |
| Local deployment | Lower network dependence and potential privacy benefits, subject to device/data security |
| Smaller scale | May struggle with broad factual knowledge/complex tasks; still can hallucinate or inherit bias |
- Source contrasts SLMs with **GPT-3**, a dated scale example; not a benchmark proving all small models inferior on every task.
- Quality of data, architecture, training and evaluation matter as well as size. SLMs are not necessarily trained only for one narrow task or on tiny datasets; a model may be general-purpose and then adapted.
- Example **Phi-3-mini**, **3.8 bn parameters**, **3.3 trillion training tokens**, demonstrates on-phone potential; example not a recommended product/current benchmark ranking. [Microsoft primary report](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/phi-3-technical-report-a-highly-capable-language-model-locally-on-your-phone/?lang=fr_ca).
- Use cases: constrained devices, task-specific assistants and local text processing; evaluate accuracy, latency, energy, privacy and failure handling in the intended setting.

topics.title: Diego Garcia and Chagos sovereignty
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Location and strategic use
- **Coral atoll**, largest/southernmost Chagos island, **central Indian Ocean**, south of equator; V-shaped land rim/open northern lagoon. Source roughly **44 km²**, **24 km length**, **11 km maximum width**, more than half BIOT land area: definitions of land/lagoon matter.
- Source report **15 Tamil Nadu fishermen detained**, alleged maritime violation; allegation/detention does not prove conviction.
- European navigation/contact in early **16th century**; “discovered” does not establish absence of earlier regional knowledge.
## Dated sovereignty sequence
- **1965**: Chagos detached from Mauritius into **British Indian Ocean Territory**; **1966 UK–US defence arrangements** for base, followed by forced removal of Chagossians.
- **2019**: ICJ advisory opinion and non-binding UN General Assembly resolution on completing Mauritius decolonisation; distinguish advisory/resolution status from a bilateral treaty.
- **October 2024** political agreement, **13 January 2025** renewed commitment to concluding a treaty: Mauritius sovereignty with long-term secure operation of UK–US Diego Garcia base proposed. It was **not already a completed January 2025 transfer**. [January joint statement](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-mauritius-joint-statement-on-the-chagos-archipelago-13-january-2025).
- Treaty **signed 22 May 2025**, envisages **99-year base arrangements**; signing and entry into force/implementation are separate. [UK signing release](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-secures-future-of-vital-diego-garcia-military-base-to-protect-national-security).
- Indian Ocean logistics/security, decolonisation, displaced people's rights and maritime jurisdiction are related but distinct issues. Dates here are historical milestones, not a claim about today's completed legal implementation.

topics.title: Makaravilakku at Sabarimala
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Ritual recall
- Annual **Sabarimala, Kerala**, **Lord Ayyappa**, **Makara Sankranti**, culmination of main pilgrimage season.
- **Thiruvabharanam**, sacred royal ornaments, brought from **Pandalam Palace**; source roughly **5,000 police** deployment in January 2025 is event-specific.
- **Ponnambalamedu** hill: ceremonial camphor flame/aarti, seen three times; source connects earlier practice to **Malayaraya** community and later management to **Travancore Devaswom Board**.
- Distinguish the **ritually lit Makaravilakku flame** from the **Makara star/Makarajyothi** in stricter usage; popular accounts sometimes interchange names. Faith interpretation is not an astronomical explanation of the human-lit flame. [Kerala Tourism festival account](https://www.keralatourism.org/1000festivals/assets/uploads/pdf/1515493142-0.pdf).
- Source describes **seven-day festival** and **Guruthi**, offering associated with wilderness deities, concluding rites; exact temple-access/closing schedules should be checked for the relevant year.
- Cultural continuity, tribal ritual heritage, crowd safety and environmental management are useful mains links.

topics.title: Clouded leopards and habitat connectivity
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species and map
| Species | Range recall |
| --- | --- |
| **Neofelis nebulosa**, mainland clouded leopard | Himalayan foothills/Northeast India, mainland Southeast Asia and southern China |
| **Neofelis diardi**, Sunda clouded leopard | **Borneo and Sumatra** |
- Source both **Vulnerable**; mainland clouded leopard **Meghalaya State animal**. Indian source locations: Sikkim/northern West Bengal and northeastern States.
- Rainforest, secondary woodland and hill habitats; Borneo mangrove examples concern the **Sunda species**, not proof mainland Indian species occurs on Borneo.
## Adaptations and conservation
- Cloud-patterned coat, pale yellow to brown ground colour; source approximate **60–110 cm**, **11–20 kg**, **12–15-year lifespan** (conditions vary).
- Long balancing tail, short legs/broad paws, exceptional climbing and headfirst descent; generally solitary. **Canine teeth longest relative to skull/body size**, not necessarily longest absolute canines of every living feline. [Smithsonian](https://www.nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/clouded-leopard).
- Taxonomically **Felidae, Pantherinae**; “neither big nor small cat” is informal language, not a separate family. Smithsonian accounts themselves differ on purring; avoid using ability to roar/purr as the defining taxonomic test.
- Study focus: habitat suitability, fragmentation and connectivity across historic/current range. Protect corridors, forest quality and prey; distinguish modelled suitable habitat from verified occupancy.

topics.title: Rat-hole mining: safety, environment and livelihoods
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Method and impacts
- Narrow coal seams/tunnels in **Meghalaya/Northeast**; small horizontal workings or pits with vertical access then narrow tunnels. Not every tunnel is simply a narrow vertical shaft.
- Rudimentary equipment, flooding, collapse, poor ventilation and hazardous/child labour; low wages and livelihood dependence compound risk.
- **East Jaintia Hills, December 2018**: **15 miners trapped after flooding**; source calls it collapse, but water ingress is central to the incident.
- Deforestation, soil erosion, acid mine drainage/coal slurry and water pollution; coal combustion adds particulates/gases but is a separate stage from extraction.
## Legal correction
- **NGT, 17 April 2014**, ordered stoppage of rat-hole/illegal mining in Meghalaya; source wrongly attributes the 2014 order to Supreme Court.
- **Supreme Court, 3 July 2019**: addressed mining/land rights and statutory compliance. Community/private mineral ownership does **not** exempt mining from **MMDR Act, 1957**, environmental approvals or safety rules. [Judgment](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/39439/39439_2018_11_1501_14662_Judgement_03-Jul-2019.pdf).
- **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**, applicable forest-conservation law, **Meghalaya Mines and Minerals Policy, 2012**; enforcement failures do not make laws legally inapplicable. Scientific permitted mining differs from continuing banned unsafe workings.
## Mains: enforce and rehabilitate
- Mine mapping/closure, transport monitoring, worker protection and responsibility; terrain, weak administration and political/economic incentives impede enforcement.
- Alternative agriculture/tourism and lawful safe livelihoods, skills/social protection, restoration and community participation; mechanisation alone does not guarantee sustainability.
- Source makes unspecific Central rehabilitation-aid claims without scheme/date: do not memorise an invented fund or entitlement.

topics.title: Central Pay Commissions and fiscal choices
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 announcement
- **16 January 2025** approval to form **8th Central Pay Commission**; source beneficiaries roughly **50 lakh employees / 65 lakh pensioners**, dated approximations, including defence personnel.
- Pay Commissions recommend pay/allowance/pension changes; government acceptance, notification and implementation are separate. Source's “7th Commission term ends 2026” conflates commission tenure with roughly decennial pay revisions.
| Commission | Constitution year / chairman |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | **1946 / Srinivasa Varadachariar** |
| 2 | **1957 / Jagannath Das** |
| 3 | **1970 / Raghubar Dayal** |
| 4 | **1983 / P. N. Singhal** |
| 5 | **1994 / S. Ratnavel Pandian** |
| 6 | **2006 / B. N. Srikrishna** |
| 7 | **2014 / A. K. Mathur** |
- Source table's **1947–59, 1959–73…2016–26** bands are not the constitution dates. [Official earlier commission chronology](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=18946).
## Speculation versus arithmetic
- Source claims proposed fitment **2.86**, but its minimum pay **₹18,000 → ₹34,560** implies **1.92**, not 2.86; 18,000 × 2.86 = **₹51,480**.
- Other printed projections **₹56,100 → ₹67,320**, **₹2.5 lakh → ₹3 lakh**, pension **₹9,000 → about ₹17,200** are inconsistent speculative scenarios, **not approved rates**. Do not infer a uniform rise or confirmed “186% hike” from thumbnail graphics.
- Later Cabinet approved **terms of reference, 28 October 2025**; distinguish that later step from the January formation announcement. [Cabinet release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2183289&lang=2&reg=48).
## Economic/ethical evaluation
- Better real wages/pensions, consumption and worker welfare versus higher recurring fiscal expenditure and potential capital-spending trade-offs; tax buoyancy/inflation/implementation phasing matter.
- Source prior 7th CPC cost **₹1 lakh crore in 2016–17**, revenue-expenditure growth **4.8% → 9.9%**, dated estimates not the new Commission's cost.
- Employee bodies raise healthcare/education/connectivity and “living wage/pension”; source **BMS, CSS Forum, AIDEF** stakeholders. Consultation with Union/States and other stakeholders; States/PSUs do not automatically implement all central recommendations.

topics.title: India–EU: trade, technology and strategic cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 editorial frame
- Partnership has substantial potential but delayed trade outcomes; pursue **economic security, defence, emerging technology, pharmaceuticals, space and critical supply chains** alongside FTA negotiations.
- Shared interests: cleaner energy, advanced manufacturing, digital innovation, quantum/biotech and public-health research; India's pharmaceutical scale and Europe's industrial/research capabilities can complement each other.
- **India–EU Trade and Technology Council (TTC)** is bilateral; **India–US iCET** is a separate mechanism. **Quad** and US Major Defence Partner designation do not automatically confer an EU defence alliance.
- Source technology claim **China leads 57/64 fields** refers to a dated research-output assessment, not mastery of every commercial technology; output, patents, manufacturing and deployment are different measures. [ASPI tracker](https://www.aspi.org.au/report/critical-technology-tracker/).
- Source proposes appointing an EU Defence Commissioner, but **Andrius Kubilius, Defence and Space Commissioner, took office December 2024**. [EU record](https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/countries/eu-enlargement-forum-2025/andrius-kubilius_en?prefLang=lt).
## Constraints → practical cooperation
- India's Russia relationship/strategic autonomy versus Europe's Ukraine concerns; both trade with China. Editorial “democracies versus autocracies” is an argument, not a binding Indian alliance doctrine.
- Trade rules/market access, standards, trust, technology-transfer terms and visas; becoming third-largest economy is a source-period projection, not an achieved January 2025 rank.
- Joint R&D/investment, skilled labour mobility, student/faculty exchanges, easier lawful visas and professional training; climate/health/security projects with measurable delivery.
- Regular summits plus institutional/community ties; democratic dialogue on misinformation, polarisation and civil liberties. Mains: acknowledge convergence and divergent interests, then propose achievable sector milestones. Daily source prompt is practice, not PYQ.

topics.title: India–Singapore and semiconductor collaboration
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Relationship timeline and corrections
- Diplomatic ties **1965**, **CECA 2005**, **Strategic Partnership 2015**, **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership September 2024**. Source's “enhanced CSP in 2022” is incorrect.
- President **Tharman Shanmugaratnam visited 14–18 January 2025**, 60th-anniversary context; semiconductor ecosystem, digital technology, healthcare and skills agreements belong to **2024 upgrade**. [MEA bilateral brief](https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-Singapore-Sep-2025.pdf).
- Diaspora source **9.1% ethnic Indian share**, **over 650,000 PIOs**, no consistent population base/date supplied; ethnic residents, PIOs and expatriate citizens differ. **Tamil** is an official language.
- Source FY2022–23 trade **US$31.6 bn**, exports/imports **16.8/14.8 bn**, sixth-partner label; FDI **US$17.2 bn**, **27%** source share. Embedded graphic uses another period: roughly **US$160 bn cumulative 2000–2024**, **24%**. Keep period and equity/total-flow definitions attached; none is today's ranking.
## Cooperation map
| Domain | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Defence | Agreement **2003**, renewed/strengthened **2015**; training at Indian facilities |
| Maritime | **SIMBEX**, white-shipping information arrangement **2017**, maritime awareness/ADMM+ |
| Digital | Fintech, payments, startups; proposed **GIFT City–Singapore financial-data corridor** |
| People | Education/research including IIT–NTU links; source **1.45 million Indian visitors, 2019** |
| Region | Gateway to ASEAN, **Act East**, near **Strait of Malacca** |
- **Singapore is not a Quad member**; regional cooperation cannot be described as its Quad membership. Data-corridor proposal is not proof an operational semiconductor production link.
## Semiconductor ecosystem: opportunities and limits
- Design → wafer fabrication → assembly/testing/packaging: each needs distinct investment/skills. Singapore experience, financing, supplier networks and training can help; Taiwan's foundry leadership must not be equated with China's position in every chip segment.
- Reliable electricity, water, clean-room quality, specialised workforce, R&D and large long-term capital; chips support autos, telecom, AI/IoT and defence. **US$5-trillion economy** is an ambition, not a guarantee delivered by one sector.
- Source eastern focus **Odisha/Assam** logistics/petrochemicals/skills is potential collaboration, not proof approved fabs in every mentioned State. Green energy/storage and efficiency reduce production footprint.
- Risks: global-cycle demand, imported equipment/IP, geopolitical disruptions, infrastructure and trade barriers. Transparent incentives, partnerships and technology capability milestones; indigenous capability does not require isolated supply chains.

topics.title: IMD at 150 and Mission Mausam
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Institution and milestone
- **India Meteorological Department**, **1875**, **Ministry of Earth Sciences**; **150th Foundation Day, 14 January 2025**, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Cyclone **Calcutta 1864** and other disasters helped motivate coordinated meteorological services.
- **Mission Mausam** and **IMD Vision 2047** launched/released at anniversary: better observation/modelling, severe-weather detection, tailored services and weather-ready/climate-smart society. [Official programme](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2092386&lang=2&reg=48).
## Source technology timeline
| Milestone | Source year |
| --- | --- |
| Indigenous radar / ISRO satellite-product collaboration | **1958 / since 1983** |
| Automatic weather stations / Doppler radar expansion | **2000 / 2010** |
| Common Alerting Protocol / impact-based forecasts | **2019 / 2019** |
| Dynamic Composite Risk Atlas | **2022** |
- Dates describe source-selected programme milestones, not proof no radar/weather station existed earlier.
- High-resolution observations, next-generation radars/satellites and **high-performance computing**; impact-based forecast asks **what weather will do**, not only its intensity.
- **Flash Flood Guidance** and regional support to Nepal/Bhutan/Bangladesh/Sri Lanka; WMO representation claim “six decades/longest Asia-Pacific” is source context, not an indefinite leadership term.
## Targets and limitations
- Source goals **accuracy +10–15% in five years**, **three-day zero-error/five-day 90% by 2047**, customised services; ambitions, not achieved guarantees. Claimed past **50% improvement** needs hazard, metric and baseline.
- Weather forecast skill ≠ short-term earthquake prediction; source's earthquake-warning aspiration should not imply reliable exact earthquake forecasts or that IMD alone performs all seismic services.
- Link early warning to last-mile communication, evacuation, agriculture/transport decisions and resilient infrastructure; forecasting alone cannot remove disaster exposure.
## Institutional recall
- Established by the **Government of India in 1875**, consolidating meteorological work under a **central authority**, rather than founded as a provincial department. Initial headquarters **Calcutta**, later Shimla → Pune → **New Delhi**. [IMD history](https://mausam.imd.gov.in/imd_latest/contents/history.php).
- **India** is a founding WMO member since **1950**; IMD is its national meteorological service, not a separate country member. The 19 January test's 1949 membership claim is incorrect. [WMO anniversary remarks](https://wmo.int/content/opening-remarks-occasion-of-imds-150th-anniversary).

topics.title: Intravenous fluids and patient safety
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## What they are
- Sterile fluids delivered **into a vein** for clinically assessed resuscitation, replacement or maintenance; not automatically needed for every sick/dehydrated person.
| Type | Contents / examples |
| --- | --- |
| **Crystalloid** | Small dissolved solutes; **normal saline, D5W (5% dextrose), lactated Ringer's** |
| **Colloid** | Larger molecules, e.g. **albumin**, synthetic starch products such as hetastarch |
- Fluid composition varies: water, sodium/chloride and sometimes glucose, potassium, calcium/lactate; not every fluid contains every electrolyte. Colloids' distribution concerns **capillary permeability**, not simply inability to cross cell membranes.
- D5W and saline have different physiological effects; colloids are not universally superior. Synthetic starch fluids have important safety restrictions; no treatment/dose recommendation follows from this recall table.
## Safety and January 2025 incident
- Source reports **12 doctors suspended in West Bengal**, Medinipur maternal/newborn deaths and alleged faulty/expired IV fluids. Suspension/allegation does not itself establish final causation or responsibility.
- Source blanket “simple, safe, low risk” is incomplete: wrong volume/composition, contamination, line infection and fluid/electrolyte overload can cause harm. Multiple fluids at one site require compatibility/clinical checks.
- Prescription by trained personnel, sterile supply-chain quality, expiry/batch traceability, assessment/reassessment and monitoring; transparent adverse-event investigation. [NICE hospital guidance](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg174/chapter/recommendations).

topics.title: Namo Drone Didi and women SHG enterprises
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Scheme: November 2024 guidelines
- **Central Sector**, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, women SHGs under **DAY-NRLM**; agricultural drone **rental services**, not free drone ownership for every farmer.
- **14,500 selected SHGs, FY2024–25 to 2025–26**; distinguish this phase from broader initial 15,000 target including earlier provision.
- Grant **80% of drone/accessories cost, maximum ₹8 lakh**; remaining finance through eligible lending, **AIF 3% interest subvention**. Maximum cap means SHG burden can exceed 20% for a higher-cost package. [Official guidelines](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2070029&lang=2&reg=3).
- Package: drone/spray assemblies, batteries, chargers, cameras/tools and supporting parts; source **up to 20 acres/day**, dependent on crop/weather/refills.
- Source pilot training **15 days**, fertiliser/pesticide applications; maintenance skill and ongoing support also matter. **Lead Fertiliser Companies**, State departments/manufacturers/SHG federations, Central Empowered Committee; MIS/Drone Portal for monitoring/funds/utilisation.
## Benefits → business viability → safeguards
- Women-led service income, rural technical skills, timely input application, labour/time savings and access to precision tools; yield gains are not guaranteed.
- Risks: repayment/utilisation, maintenance/spares, insufficient training, bureaucratic delay, chemical drift/pollinator/human exposure, notably sensitive Nilgiri habitats.
- Demand/business planning, qualified pilots, safe approved applications, no-spray buffers/weather checks, transparent monitoring and after-sales service; technology access needs environmental and livelihood safeguards.

topics.title: Supreme Court judges: appointments and independence
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional recall
- **Article 124**, originally **CJI + 7 judges**; statutory sanctioned strength **CJI + 33 = 34**, distinct from actual filled seats. January 2025 news: **Justice K. Vinod Chandran sworn in**.
- **124(3)**: Indian citizen + **5 years HC judge**, or **10 years HC advocate**, including successive qualifying HCs, or **distinguished jurist in President's opinion**. No express general minimum age in this clause.
- **124(2)**: President appoints; constitutional consultation operates through judicially developed collegium rules. Oath under **124(6)/Third Schedule**, before President/appointed person; Constitution, sovereignty/integrity, impartial duties.
- Retirement **65**; resignation to **President**. Salaries under **125**, expenditure charged to Consolidated Fund; parliamentary determination subject to constitutional protection.
- **124(7)** bars a former SC judge from pleading/acting in any court or before any authority in India. **128** recall requires CJI request, President's prior consent and **judge's consent**, not compulsory recall.
- Removal **124(4)**: President after address by **each House in same session**, majority **total membership + at least two-thirds present and voting**, **proved misbehaviour/incapacity**. Do not confuse with simple majority. [Official Constitution](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/08/7af1daa22d65f9d04c00ae9b9aa5a799.pdf).
## Collegium timeline
| Case | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| **First, 1981** | Executive primacy; consultation not binding CJI veto—source's contradictory “CJI primacy” incorrect |
| **Second, 1993** | Judicial primacy/institutional CJI opinion with two senior colleagues |
| **Third, 1998** | SC-appointment collegium **CJI + 4 senior-most** |
| **2015 NJAC judgment** | Invalidated **99th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2014**, and **NJAC Act, 2014**; collegium restored |
- “Collegium” is not constitutional text; SC appointment and HC recommendation collegia are not identical in size/function.
- Mains: independence with transparency, diversity, recorded selection criteria/conflicts and timely appointments; executive participation must respect constitutional/judicial framework.
## Distinguished jurists: proposal versus existing law
- **Article 124(3)(c)** permits a citizen whom the **President considers a distinguished jurist** to be appointed to **Supreme Court**. January article reports the route unused; this is a dated observation, not a restriction to sitting judges or practising advocates.
- **High Courts differ**: current **Article 217(2)** requires citizenship plus **ten years judicial office / ten years High Court advocacy**, with relevant counting explanations. **Article 124(3)(c) cannot directly appoint a jurist to a High Court**.
- Former **Article 217(2)(c)** jurist route was inserted by **42nd Amendment, 1976**, removed by **44th Amendment, 1978**; reintroducing it requires constitutional change. The source's combined SC/HC practice-question wording is defective. [Constitution with amendment notes](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/08/7af1daa22d65f9d04c00ae9b9aa5a799.pdf).
## Capacity and dated pendency
- Article reports **371 vacancies out of 1,122 High Court posts**, about **60 lakh HC cases**, Allahabad around **50% capacity** in its January 2025 context. These are source snapshots, not today's vacancy figures.
- Older graphic, **December 2019 → March 2022**: **SC 59,535 → 70,154; HCs 46,84,354 → 58,90,726; district/subordinate 3,22,96,224 → 4,09,85,490**. Do not label its 2019–22 chart as 2025 data.
- Chart intermediate **December 2020**: SC **64,426**, HCs **56,42,567**, district/subordinate **3,66,39,436**; **December 2021** SC **69,855**, HCs **56,49,068**. District **4,05,79,062** is printed under 2021 but footnoted **December 2020**, an internal date inconsistency.
## Evaluate the reform
- Benefits: specialist knowledge, research quality, varied perspectives, academic–practice links and expertise in complex socioeconomic/technology cases.
- Risks: limited courtroom/procedural experience, practical case management, opaque criteria and institutional resistance; merit assessment, mentoring and procedural training help.
- Source cites USA/Poland/Spain as comparisons; jurisdictions have different ordinary/constitutional court pathways, so they are not identical Indian models.
- Fill vacancies promptly while preserving independence; workload/process reform and support staff matter alongside appointments. Adding academics alone cannot erase the backlog.

topics.title: Sugary drinks and cardiometabolic disease burden
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## 2025 study: modelled attribution in 2020
- Study across **184 countries** estimated **2.2 million new type-2 diabetes cases** and **1.2 million cardiovascular-disease cases**, **2020**: **9.8% / 3.1%** of global incident cases attributable to sugar-sweetened beverages.
- These are modelled population-attributable burdens with uncertainty, not proof that a particular person's disease was caused solely by one drink. **Added-sugar beverages** include soft/energy drinks, sweetened fruit drinks/lemonade; categories/doses matter. [Primary Nature Medicine study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-024-03345-4).
| Source regional/country estimate | Diabetes / CVD attribution |
| --- | --- |
| Latin America/Caribbean | **Nearly 24% / over 11%** |
| Sub-Saharan Africa | **Over 21% diabetes** |
| Colombia / Mexico | **Over 48% / nearly one-third diabetes**, respectively |
| South Africa | **27.6% / 14.6%** |
- Sub-Saharan increase **1990–2020: 8.8 percentage points diabetes / 4.4 percentage points CVD**; percentage points ≠ relative-percent increase.
- Attributable shares vary by sex/age; higher estimates in men/younger adults do not mean older people have lower absolute cardiovascular risk in general. Income vulnerability is not a universal country-independent ranking.
## Mechanism and policy
- Liquid sugar/energy intake, limited satiety and weight gain can contribute to insulin resistance and metabolic/vascular disease; glucose spikes alone are not the entire causal pathway.
- Water access, public awareness, school/advertising safeguards, clear labelling and appropriately designed taxes; **Mexico tax, 2014**, cited consumption reduction, not instant eradication of diabetes.
- Evaluate substitution, affordability/equity, industry reformulation and long-term health outcomes alongside revenue.

topics.title: ALH Dhruv: variants, capability and safety
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Platform distinctions
- **HAL** multi-role **Advanced Light Helicopter**, roughly **5.5-tonne class**, twin-engine; high-altitude/tropical utility, troop/cargo transport, evacuation and search/rescue. Not every variant is armed or equipped for every maritime task.
| Variant | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| **Mk I / II** | Earlier utility configurations/avionics evolution |
| **Mk III** | Improved utility/mission configuration, **Shakti** engines |
| **Mk IV, Rudra** | Weapon-system-integrated version |
- **Shakti = HAL–Safran/Turbomeca collaboration**; source “Turkish T-700” is incorrect. Do not mistake Dhruv for the separate **Light Combat Helicopter Prachand**.
- Source speed **about 260 km/h**, range **600 km**, ceiling **6,500 m**, weight **5.8 tonnes** are approximate configuration figures; mission load/environment affect performance. [Official HAL platform distinction](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1565985&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source wrongly assigns generic grenade/machine-gun/rocket weapons to all Mk III craft; armed Rudra's actual fit differs. Naval/Coast Guard versions support maritime roles; ASW capability requires the specific sensors/weapons/configuration, not the name alone.
## Operators, significance and safety
- Army, Air Force, Navy, Coast Guard and civil services; source international examples **Mauritius, Nepal, Maldives**, not a complete current fleet list.
- High-altitude rescue/logistics, domestic manufacturing/supplier skills and reduced import dependence; Indian design does not imply every subsystem indigenous.
- **5 January 2025 Coast Guard crash**, source temporary grounding/inspection measures. Await inquiry findings for cause; do not assign manufacturing/operational blame solely from the crash or treat temporary grounding as permanent retirement.
- Certification, maintenance, defect reporting, transparent investigation and accountable corrective action sustain capability and public trust.

topics.title: Military expenditure and Global Firepower rankings
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Two different measures
- **SIPRI** spending estimates versus **Global Firepower** composite conventional-capability index: neither is a direct prediction of victory in a war.
- Source **2025 GFP, 145 countries, over 60 factors**; lower **Power Index** stronger by its model. Dated source top ten:
| Rank | Country | Source score |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | USA | **0.0744** |
| 2 / 3 | Russia / China | **0.0788 / 0.0788** |
| 4 / 5 | India / South Korea | **0.1184 / 0.1656** |
| 6 / 7 | UK / France | **0.1785 / 0.1878** |
| 8 / 9 / 10 | Japan / Türkiye / Italy | **0.1839 / 0.1902 / 0.2164** |
- Source puts Japan after France despite lower shown score: internal graphic discrepancy, don't independently reconstruct ranks from rounded scores. Pakistan graphic **12th, 0.2513**; Indonesia **13th**, Germany 14, Israel 15, Iran 16, Spain 17, Australia 18, Egypt 19, Ukraine 20, dated source list.
- Graphic estimates total personnel, not just active forces: USA **2,127,500**, Russia **3,570,000**, China **3,170,000**, India **5,137,550**; South Korea **3,820,000**, UK **1,108,860**, France **376,000**, Japan **328,150**, Türkiye **883,900**, Italy **289,000**. These are source model inputs, not equally defined verified active-duty counts.
## Spending and risks: dated facts
- **2023 world spending US$2,443 bn**, **+6.8% real**; India **US$83.6 bn, fourth spender, +4.2%**. [SIPRI 2023 release](https://www.sipri.org/media/press-release/2024/global-military-spending-surges-amid-war-rising-tensions-and-insecurity).
- Source **over 60 conflicts** and **civilian deaths +30%** lacks a consistent underlying dataset/year definition; distinguish number of conflicts, state-based conflicts and civilian fatalities. “Highest in history” is not established by the generic claim.
- Global Risks Report treats armed conflict as a major near-term concern; perceived risk differs from a military-capability rank.
- Mains: spending, equipment readiness, training/jointness, logistics, geography, technology and partnerships all matter; numerical manpower or spending alone cannot settle strategic outcomes.

topics.title: Nag Mk 2: fire-and-forget anti-tank missile
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Anti-armour recall
- **Third-generation, fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile (ATGM)**; indigenous DRDO development. Lock onto the target before launch; autonomous guidance thereafter reduces continued operator exposure.
- **13 January 2025, Pokhran**: three field trials at minimum/maximum ranges; demonstrated destruction of targets, including those protected by **explosive reactive armour (ERA)**. Do not confuse ERA defeat with intercepting every active-protection system.
- **NAMICA version 2** carrier evaluated alongside the missile; trials established readiness for induction, not evidence every formation had received it. [Defence release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2092585&lang=2&reg=48).
- Distinguish **Nag: anti-tank** from **Akash: surface-to-air** and **BrahMos: supersonic cruise** missile.

topics.title: Telesurgery and SSI Mantra
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Remote operation
- **Telesurgery**: surgeon controls a robotic surgical system remotely through a reliable, high-speed data link; cameras return operative images. **Tele-proctoring**: remote expert supervises/mentors, rather than directly operating.
- **January 2025 SSI Mantra 3** demonstration: Gurugram → Manipal Hospital, Jaipur, **286 km**, reported **40 ms latency**, two cardiac operations including beating-heart **Totally Endoscopic Coronary Artery Bypass (TECAB)**.
- Indigenous platform received **CDSCO approval for telesurgery/tele-proctoring**. Source's worldwide exclusivity/first claims are attributed promotional claims, not a timeless assertion about all robotic systems; a successful demonstration does not establish equal performance on every network.
- **CDSCO**, national drugs/medical-device regulator; **Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940**, with applicable device rules. Regulatory clearance differs from proof of universal clinical superiority.
## Wider healthcare robotics
| Use | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Monitoring / telepresence | Remote clinical observation and suitable sensors; cameras alone do not measure every vital sign |
| Prosthetics / exoskeletons | Mobility and rehabilitation assistance |
| Disinfection | UV-C or hydrogen-peroxide systems with exposure controls |
| Logistics | Medicines, supplies and meals |
- Cost, trained teams, latency/jitter, network redundancy, cybersecurity, informed consent, liability and local emergency backup determine safe deployment.
- Policy context: **National Health Policy 2017**; **draft National Strategy on Robotics 2023**, proposed Robotics Innovation Unit; **ARTPARK at IISc Bengaluru**. A draft/proposed unit is not automatically an operational scheme.

topics.title: Snakebite envenoming and neglected tropical diseases
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Disease and inequality
- **Envenoming**: toxin injury from venom injection; certain spitting snakes can also cause ocular exposure. Not every snakebite injects venom.
- WHO **neglected tropical disease (NTD)** portfolio since **2017**; rural/agricultural, poor and tribal communities face greater exposure and delayed care. Disability can include tissue loss/amputation, renal injury, visual impairment and psychological harm.
- India's conventional **“Big Four”**: **Indian cobra, common krait, Russell's viper, saw-scaled viper**. Important causes, but not every serious bite or region is covered by this list; “90% of all bites” is not a universal verified share.
## Dated burden: compare like with like
| Source measure | Figure / meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Karnataka reported 2024 | **13,235 cases; 101 deaths** |
| Karnataka reported 2023 | **6,596 cases; 19 deaths** |
| 2024 case hotspots | Hassan **850**, Chikkaballapur **813**, Mysuru **790** |
| 2024 death hotspots | Tumakuru **9**, Koppal **8**, Kalaburagi **8** |
- **Notifiable under Karnataka Epidemic Diseases Act, 2020**; improved **IHIP** reporting can increase recorded counts without proving true incidence doubled.
- PDF compares estimated India **3–4 million bites / about 50,000 deaths annually** with reported **~3 lakh cases / ~2,000 deaths** in 2016–20: estimates and hospital notifications are different datasets. **CBHI = Central Bureau of Health Intelligence**, not “Investigation”.
## Prevention and response
- WHO **2019 strategy**: halve **mortality and disability by 2030**; community empowerment, safe/effective treatment, stronger health systems and partnerships. [WHO strategy](https://www.who.int/publications-detail-redirect/9789241515641/).
- WHO plans include better antivenom availability, quality manufacturing and stockpiles; source **25% manufacturer increase** is a strategy target, not achieved capacity.
- India **National Action Plan for Prevention and Control of Snakebite Envenoming (NAP-SE), 12 March 2024**, **One Health** approach and target to halve deaths by 2030. Source's **2015 launch** conflicts with the actual launch. [Health Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2013803&lang=2&reg=48).
- Community education, early transport/referral, accessible quality antivenom, trained personnel and surveillance; antivenom choice/treatment requires clinical assessment.
## NTD trap
- NTDs disproportionately affect disadvantaged communities and receive insufficient research/service attention. Examples: **scabies, yaws, trachoma, leishmaniasis, Chagas disease and snakebite envenoming**.
- **Not all NTDs are infections**: snakebite is toxin-mediated. Lack of clean water/sanitation matters for several NTDs but is not the cause of every NTD.

topics.title: SVAMITVA: rural property cards and drone surveys
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Scheme identity
- **Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas (SVAMITVA)**; **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**, **Central Sector scheme**, launched **24 April 2020**, National Panchayati Raj Day; nationwide phase followed in **2021**.
- Maps **inhabited village abadi areas**, using **drones**, Survey of India surveying support, State revenue/Panchayati Raj departments and local participation. **Not a blanket cadastral survey of every agricultural field**.
- **Property cards / Record of Rights** document residential-property boundaries/rights through State legal processes. A drone image alone neither settles disputed title nor grants land to landless households.
- **18 January 2025**: about **65 lakh cards**, **50,000+ villages**, **10 States + 2 UTs**. [Official distribution brief](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/jan/doc2025118486901.pdf).
## How it helps
- Demarcation + local verification/objections → property records → fewer disputes and clearer transactions; potential bank collateral, household investment and revenue/planning for Gram Panchayats.
- GIS-based village development planning supports roads, water, drainage and service allocation; this is **rural**, not principally urban planning.
- Credit access remains subject to legal enforceability and lending assessment; property cards do not guarantee a loan.
## Implementation safeguards
- Pilot in selected States, then phased expansion; source 2025 full-coverage ambition is a target, not proof all villages surveyed/cards issued.
- Accurate survey/georeferencing, resolve old-record conflicts, public notice and grievance access; ensure women/co-owners and marginalised residents are correctly recorded.
- Coordinate Survey of India, State departments and Gram Panchayats; protect personal/property data, train staff and maintain records after transactions.
- Mains: technology enables tenure security only when supported by **law, verification, inclusion and ongoing record updates**.

topics.title: Konark Sun Temple: Kalinga architecture
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Core recall
- **Surya / Sun Temple**, **Konark, Puri district, Odisha**, Bay of Bengal coast; **Narasimhadeva I**, **Eastern Ganga dynasty**, mid-13th century (**c.1250**; reign 1238–64).
- **UNESCO World Heritage, 1984**; culmination of **Kalinga/Odisha temple architecture**, within the broader Nagara tradition. “Kalinga” and “Nagara” need not be mutually exclusive answer choices.
- Monument conceived as Surya's chariot: **24 wheels = 12 pairs**, intended **seven horses**. PDF says six; UNESCO's short description also says six, but its detailed outstanding-value statement specifies seven. Use **seven for original symbolism**, distinguish surviving sculptures. [UNESCO record](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/246/).
## Architecture and sculpture
- East-oriented; surviving **Jagamohana** assembly hall, ruined principal sanctuary (**vimana/deul**) and dance hall (**natamandira**). Source's “100-foot” figure should not describe the entire original tower indiscriminately.
- Carved wheels can indicate solar time; reject universal minute-perfect accuracy under all conditions.
- **Khondalite** is a major building stone; other materials occur too. Sculpture: deities/myths, animals, foliage, musicians/dancers, warriors and social life.
- Historic name **Black Pagoda**; counterpart **White Pagoda: Jagannath Temple, Puri**. Do not infer the whole monument is made of black granite.
- **Chandrabhaga / Magha Saptami** traditions in the area; distinguish religious association from assuming routine worship continues inside the ruined main sanctuary.
## Conservation
- Salt-laden air, erosion/cyclones, biological weathering, structural weakness and tourism pressure; ASI conservation and protected/regulatory zones.

topics.title: Bharat Mobility and green transport
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 expo
- **Bharat Mobility Global Expo, 17–22 January 2025**, opened **17 January**, three venues: **Bharat Mandapam, Yashobhoomi (Delhi), India Expo Centre & Mart (Greater Noida)**. Source says five-day; official dates span six days.
- **Seven Cs**: **Common, Connected, Convenient, Congestion-free, Charged, Clean, Cutting-edge**. Shared mobility, integration, accessibility and cleaner technology work together.
- Dated speech: India **third-largest automobile market**; source specifies passenger-vehicle market. Ranking metric must be clear; January description **fifth-largest economy** is dated.
## Source figures: don't mix denominators
| Figure | Qualification |
| --- | --- |
| ~2.5 crore vehicles; ~12% growth | Source 2024 sales, across vehicle categories |
| 16.8 lakh EVs versus ~2,600 a decade earlier | Roughly **640-fold**, not **640%** |
| Eightfold EV-sales growth by 2030 | Projection, not completed growth |
| ₹11 lakh crore infrastructure | Budgeted/announced capital-expenditure context, not proof exact realised auto-sector spending |
| 100+ launches, 5,100 international participants, 5 lakh visitors | Event publicity/expected attendance; expectations differ from final counts |
| 1.5 lakh jobs; ₹2.25 lakh crore sales | Source PLI figures without a clear auto-only scheme denominator; do not present as audited auto-PLI outcomes |
- Correct dates and growth unit: [Official inaugural account](https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/pm-inaugurates-bharat-mobility-global-expo-2025/).
## Policy and trade-offs
- EVs, hydrogen and biofuels aim to reduce oil dependence/emissions; **National Electric Mobility Mission**, **National Green Hydrogen Mission**, manufacturing **PLI**, charging infrastructure and scrappage policy.
- **PM Gati Shakti**, highways and multimodal logistics can lower transport costs. Demand, domestic components, skills, R&D and export competitiveness support industry.
- EVs eliminate tailpipe emissions, but total benefit depends on electricity mix, battery sourcing/recycling and vehicle use. Public transport and walkability also reduce congestion; replacing every car with an EV alone does not.

topics.title: Gulf of Aden: chokepoints and maritime security
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map recall
- Between **Yemen / Arabian Peninsula (north)** and **Somalia / Horn of Africa (south)**; **Djibouti** at western approach, **Arabian Sea** to east. **Socotra belongs to Yemen**, near the eastern approach.
- **Arabian Sea → Gulf of Aden → Bab el-Mandeb → Red Sea → Suez Canal → Mediterranean**. Gulf of Aden does not directly open into the Mediterranean.
- **Guardafui Channel**: between northeastern Somalia and Socotra; **Gulf of Tadjoura**: western inlet in Djibouti. **Hormuz** connects Persian Gulf/Gulf of Oman, not Aden/Red Sea.
- Source dimensions roughly **900 km × 500 km**, area **410,000 km²**; approximate boundary-dependent measures. **Sheba Ridge**, active spreading system; salinity generally lower than the highly evaporative Red Sea.
- Ports/cities: **Aden, Mukalla, Ahwar, Balhaf (Yemen); Berbera, Bosaso (Somali coast); Djibouti City**.
## Security and economy
- Suez route vital for Asia–Europe commerce, energy and container shipping. Source **11% of seaborne petroleum** lacks a reference year/definition; avoid treating as an unchanging flow.
- Piracy, attacks on shipping and regional conflict threaten vessels and raise insurance/freight costs; diversions around the Cape lengthen voyages.
- Indian naval patrols, maritime-domain awareness, escorts/rescue and partner information-sharing; protect commerce while following international law and avoiding escalation.

topics.title: Lokpal: jurisdiction, composition and safeguards
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- **Statutory**, not constitutional: **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013**; commencement **16 January 2014**. First Foundation Day celebration **16 January 2025**, Delhi; commencement differs from first appointments.
- **Chairperson + up to eight members**; **50% judicial members**, **not less than 50% of members collectively from SC/ST/OBC/minorities/women**. Not a separate 50% quota for each group.
- Chair: former **CJI**, former **Supreme Court judge**, or eligible eminent person; judicial member: former **SC judge / High Court Chief Justice**. Eminent members require relevant expertise and statutory eligibility, not simply fame.
- **President** appoints on committee recommendation: **PM (chair), Lok Sabha Speaker, Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition, CJI or nominated SC judge, eminent jurist**.
- **Five years or age 70**, whichever earlier; Chair remuneration equivalent to **CJI**, members to **SC judges**. [Act and sections](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/2122?col=123456789%2F1362).
## Jurisdiction and exclusions
- Corruption offences under **Prevention of Corruption Act**: **PM, Union ministers, MPs, Central Groups A–D**, covered government-funded/controlled entities; qualifying foreign-contribution recipients above **₹10 lakh annually**.
- MPs' protected parliamentary speech/votes excluded; PM allegations concerning **international relations, external/internal security, public order, atomic energy and space** excluded.
- PM inquiry needs **full bench**, approval of **at least two-thirds**; in-camera proceedings and confidentiality safeguards apply. “PM entirely exempt” is incorrect.
- Complaint rules/form and statutory time limits apply; “any person may complain” does not mean every complaint is admissible regardless of content or age.
## Inquiry and powers
- Preliminary inquiry or investigation by authorised agency including **CBI**; **CVC route** for specified Central servant categories: Group **A/B** reports back to Lokpal; Group **C/D** proceeds under CVC powers with reporting/oversight.
- Lokpal supervises **CBI cases referred by it**, not every CBI case; investigating-officer transfer requires its approval in covered cases.
- Civil-court-type inquiry powers, searches, provisional attachment, record protection and recommendations for transfer/suspension. **Final confiscation is through Special Court**, not unrestricted direct Lokpal confiscation.
- Annual report to **President**, laid before **Parliament**; effectiveness needs staff, independent investigations, timely follow-up and due process.

topics.title: La Pérouse: multinational naval interoperability
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Exercise recall
- **French Navy-led multinational maritime exercise**, Indo-Pacific/Indian Ocean approaches; **INS Mumbai**, indigenous guided-missile destroyer, participated in January 2025.
- PIB labels 2025 **fourth edition**; French Navy release calls it **fifth**. Keep institutional discrepancy visible rather than silently settling it. [Indian Navy release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2093998&lang=2&reg=48), [French Navy account](https://www.defense.gouv.fr/marine/actualites/clemenceau-25-gan-lance-lexercice-multinational-perouse-25-detroits-reliant-oceans-indien).
- Source participants besides India: **France, Australia, UK, USA, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Canada**; not Russia. Nine nations including India.
- Maritime situational awareness, surveillance/interdiction, information-sharing and interoperability; surface/air defence, tactical manoeuvres, cross-deck landings and **VBSS: Visit, Board, Search and Seizure**.
- Supports **SAGAR: Security and Growth for All in the Region**, safe sea lanes and rules-based maritime cooperation; a naval exercise is not a bilateral trade agreement or binding alliance.

topics.title: IMEC: India–Middle East–Europe connectivity
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Proposed corridor
- **India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor**, MoU announced at **G20 New Delhi, September 2023**; **proposed ship-to-rail network**, not an already completed continuous rail route.
- **East corridor: India ↔ Arabian Gulf**; **Northern corridor: Gulf ↔ Europe**. Rail and maritime legs supplement existing sea/road routes, with planned **electricity/data cables and clean-hydrogen pipeline**.
- MoU participants: **India, USA, Saudi Arabia, UAE, EU, France, Germany, Italy**. **Jordan and Israel** appear on envisaged transit alignment but are not among the eight MoU participants. [Commerce Ministry parliamentary reply](https://commerce.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/LS-USQ-No.715-dt.-07.02.2024.pdf).
- **Practice-key correction:** shipping is integral. The PDF wrongly excludes maritime lanes while accepting cables/pipeline; its listed options lack the complete **A+B+D+E** combination. Nuclear plants are not a specified core component.
## Source map: indicative ports, not a final binding route
| Region | Source-listed nodes |
| --- | --- |
| India | **Mundra, Kandla/Deendayal (Gujarat); JNPT/JNPA (Navi Mumbai)** |
| UAE | **Fujairah, Jebel Ali, Abu Dhabi** |
| Saudi Arabia | **Dammam, Ras Al Khair** |
| Transit / Israel | Saudi Arabia → **Jordan → Haifa** |
| Europe | **Piraeus (Greece), Messina (Italy), Marseille (France)** |
- A particular map alignment is not proof every port or rail link was finalised in the founding MoU.
## Why it matters
- Diversified Asia–Europe trade, Gulf partnerships, port/logistics/manufacturing investment, possible SEZs, energy/digital links and jobs; geopolitical alternative to **BRI**, without implying every participant shares an anti-China alliance.
- Source **40% faster** and **US$3–8 bn cost** are estimates without a settled route/financial baseline, not guaranteed realised savings or a final whole-project budget.
- Potential “infrastructure for peace” needs actual diplomatic stability; prospective Africa extensions are not an existing IMEC leg.
## Challenges and way forward
- Missing rail links, port capacity and **ship↔rail transshipment**; customs documentation, gauges/technical standards, tariffs and multimodal scheduling.
- Financing, commercial viability, Israel–regional conflict, infrastructure protection, environmental impact and country-specific laws.
- Phase viable segments; agree interoperable systems and customs rules, transparent funding/risk allocation, resilient energy/data links and partner consultation. IMEC complements other routes rather than guaranteeing elimination of Suez traffic.

topics.title: Colonial wealth extraction and inequality
topics.subject: Modern Indian History
topics.markdown:
## Oxfam: Takers, Not Makers (2025)
- Report links inherited fortunes, colonial exploitation and contemporary global inequality; arguments/statistics belong to the **2025 report**, not a neutral audited historical cash ledger.
- Estimate of India→UK extraction **1765–1900: US$64.82 trillion**; **US$33.8 trillion**, roughly **52%**, attributed to Britain's richest **10%**.
- **Method matters**: estimates of historical drain are **cumulated to 2020** in dollar terms; not simply the amount actually transferred in nineteenth-century dollars. Methodology contrasts **US$1.925 trillion cumulated to 1947**. Results depend on assumptions and compounding. [Oxfam methodology](https://www.oxfamfrance.org/app/uploads/2025/01/Oxfam-Davos-2025-Methodology-Note.pdf).
- Illustration that elite share could cover London in £50 notes nearly four times is an analogy, not an additional independent measurement. [Oxfam report summary](https://laos.oxfam.org/latest/publications/takers-not-makers).
## Mechanisms and historical connection
- Colonial revenue extraction, land/resource control, trade rules and labour exploitation transferred surplus abroad; raw-material exports and unequal market access constrained domestic development.
- **East India Company** combined commercial power and political coercion; important precursor to multinational networks, without treating all modern corporations as legally identical colonial rulers.
- Connect to **drain-of-wealth critique**: domestic surplus used abroad rather than reinvested locally. Different historical scholars' estimates must retain their period/method labels.
## Contemporary debate
- Oxfam links Global South labour/resource extraction to profits accruing in Global North; distinguish historical influence from assuming every present transaction has the same colonial mechanism.
- Proposed responses: effective progressive/wealth taxation, fairer labour/trade rules, debt relief, institutional reform, acknowledgement/reparations.
- Mains: explain mechanisms and distributional effects, assess methodology, and compare remedies for feasibility and equity; do not present reparations proposals as enacted policy.
